options: Accounting as a language of business can be viewed as an information system that provides essential information about economic activities of an entity to various individuals and groups.
It is the role of the accounting system to provide economic information for users on which to base their decisions concerning the allocation of the scarce resources
The goal (objective) of accounting is to identify, analyze, record, report, and interpret (communicate) economic data for use by decision makers.
Management accounting is the accounting area that intends to serve information needs of external users.
questions.correctAnswer: Management accounting is the accounting area that intends to serve information needs of external users.
questions.explanation: Financial accounting serves external users. Management accounting is for internal decision-making (managers).

questions.questionText: One of the following statements is incorrect.
options: Revenue recognition principle requires that companies recognize/record revenue in the accounting period in which the performance obligation is satisfied.
Going concern assumption requires that the activities of the entity be kept separate and distinct from the activities of its owner and any other economic entities.
Selection of which measurement principle of accounting to record and report transactions to follow generally relates to trade-offs between relevance and faithful representation.

The periodicity assumption implies that a company can divide its economic activities into artificial time periods to communicate to users who need to know a company‘s performance and economic status on a timely basis.
questions.correctAnswer: Going concern assumption requires that the activities of the entity be kept separate and distinct from the activities of its owner and any other economic entities.
questions.explanation: That statement describes the economic entity assumption. Going concern assumes the business will continue operating for the foreseeable future.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is false?
options: Double-entry system is a system that records the dual effect of each transaction in appropriate accounts.
Normal balance an account is the side where a decrease in the account is recorded.
Accrual-basis accounting is accounting basis in which companies record transactions that change a company’s financial statements in the periods in which the events occur.
An account is an individual accounting record of increases and decreases in specific asset, liability, and equity items.
questions.correctAnswer: Normal balance an account is the side where a decrease in the account is recorded.
questions.explanation: Normal balance is the side that records increases (debit for assets/expenses/drawings; credit for liabilities/equity/revenues). The opposite side records decreases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a resource that a business organization owns and possesses the capacity to provide future services or economic benefits?
questions.explanation: Definition of assets per conceptual framework: resources controlled by the entity as a result of past events and from which future economic benefits are expected.

questions.questionText: Desta decide to open a computer service company on September 1, 2014, he invest €60,000 cash in the business in exchange for €60,000 of ordinary shares. This transaction result in;
questions.explanation: Owner investment increases assets (cash) and increases equity (share capital/owner's capital). No receivable, liability or equipment is involved.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In order to ensure high-quality financial reporting, accountants present financial statements in conformity with accounting standards that are issued by standard setting bodies.
The fair value principle states that assets and liabilities should be reported at fair value (the price received to sell an asset or settle a liability).
Relevance and faithful representation are two primary qualities that make accounting information useful for decision-making.
Relevance means that the numbers and descriptions match what really existed or happened they are factual.
questions.correctAnswer: Relevance means that the numbers and descriptions match what really existed or happened they are factual.
questions.explanation: That describes faithful representation (complete, neutral, free from error). Relevance = information capable of influencing decisions (predictive + confirmatory value).

questions.questionText: Hello Company buys a $30,000 car on credit. The transaction will affect the statement;
questions.explanation: Asset (car) ↑ and liability (payable) ↑ → affects only balance sheet (statement of financial position). No immediate income, equity change (except through future depreciation), or cash flow.

questions.questionText: The accounting part that intends to serve accounting information needs of external users.
questions.explanation: Financial accounting produces general-purpose financial statements for external users (investors, creditors, regulators). Management & cost accounting primarily serve internal users.

questions.questionText: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is considered to be more:
questions.explanation: IFRS provides broad principles and requires professional judgment. US GAAP is more detailed and rule-oriented.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is false?
options: A statement of cash flows summarizes information about the cash inflows (receipts) and outflows (payments) for a specific period of time.
A statement of financial position reports the assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific date.
A retained earnings statement summarizes the changes in retained earnings for a specific period of time.
An income statement presents the revenues, expenses, changes in equity, and resulting net income or net loss for a specific period of time.
questions.correctAnswer: An income statement presents the revenues, expenses, changes in equity, and resulting net income or net loss for a specific period of time.
questions.explanation: Income statement shows revenues, expenses → net income/loss. Changes in equity are shown in statement of changes in equity / retained earnings statement.

questions.questionText: One of the following is different
questions.explanation: Dividend, share capital and liabilities are balance sheet items (equity or liability). Expenses are income statement (temporary) accounts.

questions.questionText: In Accounting Companies initially record transactions in chronological order. Here the phrase chronological order, implies?
options: The order of transactions based on their transaction size.
The order in which business transactions occur.
The sequence in which financial statement items are presented.
The serially ordered number of records where transactions appear.
questions.correctAnswer: The order in which business transactions occur.
questions.explanation: Journal entries are recorded in date order (chronological) — the sequence events actually happened.

questions.questionText: Determine the ending balance in cash for cash account of the general ledger after posting. The beginning balance on March 1 was ETB 6000; on March 4 debited cash for ETB 2580 from sales of services; on March 15 paid ETB 4000 for salaries and wages expense; on March 19 paid ETB 920 for utilities expense.
A trial balance:
options: Is the same under GAAP and IFRS
Proves that transactions are recorded correctly.
Proves that all transactions have been recorded.
Will not balance if a correct journal entry is posted twice.
questions.correctAnswer: Will not balance if a correct journal entry is posted twice.
questions.explanation: Posting the same correct entry twice doubles both debit and credit → trial balance still balances (but amounts are wrong). Trial balance proves equality of debits & credits, not completeness or correctness of amounts.

questions.questionText: The general policy for using proper currency signs (Birr, dollar, yen, pound, etc.) is the same for both GAAP and IFRS. This policy is:
options: Currency signs only appear in ledgers and journal entries.
Currency signs are only shown in the trial balance.
Currency signs are shown for all compound journal entries.
Currency signs are shown in trial balances and financial statements.
questions.correctAnswer: Currency signs are shown in trial balances and financial statements.
questions.explanation: Both frameworks require currency denomination in financial statements and trial balance. Journal/ledger entries often omit symbols for brevity.

questions.questionText: The trial balance of CCC Corporation had accounts with the following normal balances: Cash $5,000, Service Revenue $85,000, Salaries and Wages Payable $4,000, Salaries and Wages Expense $40,000, Rent Expense $10,000, Share Capital— Ordinary $42,000, Dividends $15,000 and Equipment $61,000. In preparing a trial balance, the total in the debit column is:
questions.explanation: Debits: Cash 5,000 + Expense 40,000 + Rent 10,000 + Equipment 61,000 + Dividends 15,000 = 131,000. (Revenue and capital are credits; payable is credit.)

questions.questionText: One difference between GAAP and IFRS is that:
options: IFRS uses accrual- concepts, and GAAP uses primarily the cash basis of accounting.
GAAP uses a different journal, ledger and posting process than IFRS.
IFRS uses more fair value measurements than GAAP.
The double-entry accounting system is different between GAAP and IFRS.
questions.correctAnswer: IFRS uses more fair value measurements than GAAP.
questions.explanation: Both use accrual accounting and double-entry. IFRS generally permits/requires more fair value (e.g. investment property, certain financial instruments) than rules-based US GAAP.

questions.questionText: TAT hires five employees on Nov.5, to begin work on Nov. 8. Each employee is to receive a weekly salary of 1000 Birr for a five day work week (Monday to Friday), payable every two weeks – first payment will be made on Nov. 19. How much employee salary does TAT owes and pays in cash on Nov.?
questions.explanation: No work performed before Nov. 8 → no salary earned or paid in November up to the question's implied date. First payment Nov. 19 covers Nov. 8–19 work.

questions.questionText: When will be the second pay day?
questions.explanation: Payable every two weeks. First pay Nov. 19 → second pay = Nov. 19 + 14 days = Dec. 3.

questions.questionText: How much is accrued salaries, assuming adjusting entries are dated November 30?
questions.explanation: 5 employees × 1000 Birr/week = 5000/week. From Nov. 26–30 (5 days) = one full week owed but unpaid at Nov. 30 → 5000 + 2000 (Nov. 22–25 already paid on Nov. 19? Wait — standard calculation: typically 7,000 if partial weeks considered. Many solutions use 5×1000 + 2×1000 = 7000 for the unpaid period after last payment.

questions.questionText: Debits:
questions.explanation: Debits increase assets and expenses, decrease liabilities, equity and revenues.

questions.questionText: Accounts that normally have debit balances are:
questions.explanation: Normal debit balances: Assets, Expenses, Drawings (contra-equity). Revenues, capital and liabilities normally have credit balances.

questions.questionText: Adjustments for unearned revenues:
options: Have an assets and revenues account relationship.
questions.explanation: Unearned revenue (liability) → when earned: debit liability, credit revenue.

questions.questionText: The receipt of cash from customers in payment of their accounts would be recorded by:
options: A debit to Cash and a credit to Accounts Receivable.
A debit to Accounts Receivable and a credit to Cash.
A debit to Cash and a credit to Accounts Payable.
A debit to Accounts Payable and a credit to Cash.
questions.correctAnswer: A debit to Cash and a credit to Accounts Receivable.
questions.explanation: Cash increases (debit), receivable decreases (credit).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about the accrual basis of accounting is false?
options: Events that change a company’s financial position are recorded in the periods in which the events occur.
Revenue is recognized in the period in which services are performed.
The accrual basis is in accordance with IFRS.
Revenue and expense are recorded only when cash is received, or only when cash is paid.
questions.correctAnswer: Revenue and expense are recorded only when cash is received, or only when cash is paid.
questions.explanation: That describes cash basis. Accrual basis records when earned/incurred, regardless of cash movement.

questions.questionText: An accrued expense is an expense
questions.explanation: Accrued expense = expense recognized before cash payment (e.g. unpaid salaries, interest).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct statement about revenue recognition principle
options: A company recognizes revenue when it agrees to perform a service or sell a product to a customer.
Requires that companies recognize revenue in the accounting period in which they receive cash.
Revenue shall be recognized in the accounting period in which the performance obligation is satisfied.
It is based on a simple rule, “Let the revenue follow the expenses”
questions.correctAnswer: Revenue shall be recognized in the accounting period in which the performance obligation is satisfied.
questions.explanation: Core principle of IFRS 15 / modern revenue standards: recognize when control transfers (performance obligation satisfied).

questions.questionText: The purchase of supplies on account should result in:
options: A debit to Accounts payable and a credit to Cash.
A debit to cash and a credit to Accounts Payable.
A debit to Supplies and a credit to Accounts Payable.
A debit to Supplies and a credit to Accounts Receivable.
questions.correctAnswer: A debit to Supplies and a credit to Accounts Payable.
questions.explanation: Asset (supplies) ↑ debit, liability (payable) ↑ credit.

questions.questionText: In accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards, Revenue and Expense Recognition principles are defined, what does recognition implies in this context?
options: To enter in to a contract with a customer.
questions.explanation: Recognition = when an item meets definition and measurement criteria and is included in financial statements.

questions.questionText: Companies record transactions in the period in which the events occur.
questions.explanation: Accrual basis records revenues/expenses when earned/incurred, not when cash moves.

questions.questionText: Expenses paid in cash before they are used or consumed.
questions.explanation: Prepaid = asset created when payment made in advance (e.g. insurance, rent paid ahead).

questions.questionText: Identify correct statement regarding periodicity assumption
options: An assumption requiring companies to use calendar year (Jan. 1 to Dec. 31) as their accounting time period.
It is also called time period assumption, in which accountants divide the economic life of a business in to artificial time periods (like a month, a quarter or a year).
It states the company’s year-end shall not vary from year to year.
Divides accounting time period in to a period that is one year in length known as – fiscal year only.
questions.correctAnswer: It is also called time period assumption, in which accountants divide the economic life of a business in to artificial time periods (like a month, a quarter or a year).
questions.explanation: Periodicity (time period) assumption allows reporting in artificial periods for timely information. Companies may choose fiscal year ≠ calendar year.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is incorrect concerning the adjusted trial balance?
options: An adjusted trial balance proves the equality of the total debit balances and the total credit balances in the ledger after all adjustments are made.
The adjusted trial balance provides the primary basis for the preparation of financial statements.
The adjusted trial balance lists the account balances segregated by assets and liabilities.
The adjusted trial balance is prepared after the adjusting entries have been journalized and posted.
questions.correctAnswer: The adjusted trial balance lists the account balances segregated by assets and liabilities.
questions.explanation: Adjusted trial balance lists all accounts with their adjusted balances (not segregated by category — that happens in financial statements).

questions.questionText: The trial balance shows Supplies $0 and Supplies Expense $1,500. If $800 of supplies are on hand at the end of the period, the adjusting entry is:
options: Debit Supplies $800 and credit Supplies Expense $800.
Debit Supplies Expense $800 and credit Supplies $800.
Debit Supplies $700 and credit Supplies Expense $700.
Debit Supplies Expense $700 and credit Supplies $700.
questions.correctAnswer: Debit Supplies $800 and credit Supplies Expense $800.
questions.explanation: Expense overstated by amount still on hand → reduce expense, increase asset: Dr Supplies 800, Cr Supplies Expense 800.

questions.questionText: Identify the incorrect statement
options: Closing entries produce a zero balance in each temporary account.
If total debits exceed total credits in the income statement columns of the worksheet. In that case, the company has a net loss.
The purpose of the post-closing trial balance is to prove the equality of the permanent and temporary account balances carried forward into the next accounting period.
As a required step in the accounting cycle firms should correct errors, as soon as they discover them, by journalizing and posting correcting entries.
questions.correctAnswer: The purpose of the post-closing trial balance is to prove the equality of the permanent and temporary account balances carried forward into the next accounting period.
questions.explanation: Post-closing trial balance contains only permanent (real) accounts. Temporary accounts have been closed to zero.

questions.questionText: Gross profit will result if:
options: Operating expenses are less than net income.
Sales revenues are greater than operating expenses.
Sales revenues are greater than cost of goods sold.
Operating expenses are greater than cost of goods sold.
questions.correctAnswer: Sales revenues are greater than cost of goods sold.
questions.explanation: Gross profit = Sales − Cost of Goods Sold. Operating expenses are deducted later to get operating income.

questions.questionText: Under a perpetual inventory system, when goods are purchased for resale by a company:
options: Purchases account are debited to Merchandise Inventory.
Purchases on account are debited to Purchases.
Purchase returns are debited to Purchase Returns and Allowances.
Freight costs are debited to Freight-out
questions.correctAnswer: Purchases account are debited to Merchandise Inventory.
questions.explanation: Perpetual: inventory account is updated continuously. Purchase → Dr Inventory, Cr Cash/Payable.

questions.questionText: The sales accounts that normally have a debit balance are:
questions.explanation: Both are contra-revenue accounts (debit balances) that reduce gross sales to net sales.

questions.questionText: A credit sale of $750 is made on June 13, terms 2/10, net/30. A return of $50 is granted on June 16.The amount received as payment in full on June 23 is:
questions.explanation: Net amount after return: 750 − 50 = 700. 2% discount within 10 days: 700 × 0.02 = 14. Cash received = 700 − 14 = 686.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accounts will normally appear in the ledger of a merchandising company that uses a perpetual inventory system?
questions.explanation: Perpetual system uses Inventory and Cost of Goods Sold accounts. Purchases, freight-in, discounts are periodic system accounts.

questions.questionText: To record the sale of goods for cash in a perpetual inventory system:
options: Only one journal entry is necessary to record cost of goods sold and reduction of inventory.
Only one journal entry is necessary to record the receipt of cash and the sales revenue.
Two journal entries are necessary: one to record the receipt of cash and sales revenue, and one to record the cost of goods sold and reduction of inventory.
Two journal entries are necessary: one to record the receipt of cash and reduction of inventory, and one to record the cost of goods sold and sales revenue
questions.correctAnswer: Two journal entries are necessary: one to record the receipt of cash and sales revenue, and one to record the cost of goods sold and reduction of inventory.
questions.explanation: Perpetual requires separate entry for revenue (Dr Cash, Cr Sales) and cost (Dr COGS, Cr Inventory).

questions.questionText: The steps in the accounting cycle for a merchandising company are the same as those in a service company except:
options: An additional adjusting journal entry for inventory may be needed in a merchandising company.
Closing journal entries are not required for a merchandising company.
A post-closing trial balance is not required for a merchandising company.
A multiple-step income statement is required for a merchandising company
questions.correctAnswer: An additional adjusting journal entry for inventory may be needed in a merchandising company.
questions.explanation: Periodic system needs year-end inventory adjustment and COGS calculation. Perpetual usually does not.

questions.questionText: The multiple-step income statement for a merchandising company shows each of the following features except:
questions.explanation: Investing activities appear in statement of cash flows, not income statement.

questions.questionText: When goods are purchased for resale by a company using a periodic inventory system:
options: Purchases on account are debited to Merchandise Inventory.
Purchases on account are debited to Purchases.
Purchase returns are debited to Purchase Returns and Allowances.
Freight costs are debited to Purchases
questions.correctAnswer: Purchases on account are debited to Purchases.
questions.explanation: Periodic system uses Purchases account (not Inventory) during the period.

questions.questionText: In determining cost of goods sold:
options: Purchase discounts are deducted from net purchases.
Freight-out is added to net purchases.
Purchase returns and allowances are deducted from net purchases.
Freight-in is added to net purchases
questions.correctAnswer: Freight-in is added to net purchases
questions.explanation: COGS (periodic) = Beg Inv + Net Purchases + Freight-in − Ending Inv. Freight-in is part of cost of purchases.

questions.questionText: A company has cash sales of $75,000, credit sales of $320,000, sales returns and allowances of $13,700, and sales discounts of $6,000. Its net sales equal
If merchandise purchased on account is returned, the buyer may inform the seller of the details by issuing
questions.explanation: Buyer issues debit memo (reduce payable). Seller issues credit memo (reduce receivable).

questions.questionText: The income statement in which the total of all expenses is deducted from the total of all revenues is termed:
questions.explanation: Single-step subtracts total expenses from total revenues in one step. Multiple-step shows gross profit, operating income, etc.

questions.questionText: Which of the following expenses would normally be classified as other expense on a multiple-step income statement?
questions.explanation: Interest expense is non-operating (other expense). Operating expenses include selling & admin (depreciation, salaries, insurance).

questions.questionText: A kind of inventory system which updates accounting records for each purchase and each sale of inventory is
questions.explanation: Perpetual continuously updates Inventory and COGS accounts with every transaction.

questions.questionText: ____________ refers to a seller granting a price reduction (allowance) to a buyer of defective or unacceptable merchandise.
questions.explanation: Allowance = price reduction without returning goods. Return = goods sent back.

questions.questionText: In FOB shipping point agreement, which of the following is true:
options: ownership of goods transfers to the buyer when the goods arrive at the buyer’s place of business
The buyer accepts ownership when the goods depart the seller’s place of business
The seller pays shipping costs and has the risk of loss in transit
The goods are part of the seller’s inventory when they are in transit
questions.correctAnswer: The buyer accepts ownership when the goods depart the seller’s place of business
questions.explanation: FOB shipping point = title passes at seller's dock → buyer owns goods in transit and bears risk/loss.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is true about expenses incurred by merchandising business
options: Selling expenses are the expenses of advertising merchandise, making sales, and delivering goods to customers.
General and administrative expenses support a company’s overall operations and include expenses related to accounting, human resources, and finance
Other expenses and losses commonly do not include interest expense, losses from asset disposals, and casualty losses
Operating expenses are separated into two parts selling and General and Administrative expense.
questions.correctAnswer: Operating expenses are separated into two parts selling and General and Administrative expense.
questions.explanation: Multiple-step income statement classifies operating expenses as (1) selling and (2) general & administrative. Other options contain inaccuracies.

questions.questionText: Except one All are the basic elements of an accounting system
questions.explanation: Basic elements: source documents, input devices, processor, storage, output. Internet is a communication tool, not core component.

questions.questionText: Computer software that controls the computer hardware and makes hardware respond the user’s needs is?
questions.explanation: System software (OS, drivers) manages hardware and provides platform for application software (e.g. Peachtree = accounting application).

questions.questionText: One of the following is not accounting applications software?
questions.explanation: STATA is statistical/econometric software. Others are accounting packages.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not true regarding computerized accounting system?
options: It is an accounting system that performs data processing manually
It increases efficiency, accuracy, speed and timeliness
It enables to handle complex and large transactions easily
It reduces cost in relation to record keeping (cost per transaction)
questions.correctAnswer: It is an accounting system that performs data processing manually
questions.explanation: Computerized system processes data electronically (automatically), not manually.

questions.questionText: Which method should be selected if you want to recognize revenue when earned and expense when incurred?
questions.explanation: Accrual basis matches revenues earned and expenses incurred in the same period, regardless of cash timing.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following cannot be taken as difference between manual and computerized systems?
questions.explanation: Both systems record the same accounting meaning/principles. Differences are in speed, accuracy, backup ease, processing method — not conceptual meaning.

questions.questionText: ______ is a system that interprets, transforms and summarizes information for use in analysis and reporting.
questions.explanation: Information processor = component that classifies, calculates, summarizes data (computer CPU or manual processing).

questions.questionText: A group of related accounts showing the details of the balance of general ledger accounts are
questions.explanation: Subsidiary ledgers (e.g. accounts receivable ledger) provide detailed breakdown; control account in general ledger shows total.

questions.questionText: What does it mean by saving your data permanently in data storage devices?
questions.explanation: Backup = copying data to secure storage for recovery if original is lost/damaged.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct match
options: Sales Journal- For recording credit sales
Purchase journal- For recording cash purchase
Special Journal – For recording detail balance
Payment Journal – For recording credit purchase
questions.correctAnswer: Sales Journal- For recording credit sales
questions.explanation: Sales journal records credit sales of inventory. Cash sales go to cash receipts journal. Purchase journal is for credit purchases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered cash?
questions.explanation: Cash equivalents include highly liquid investments with insignificant risk of change in value and maturity ≤ 3 months. Money market checking accounts qualify. CDs usually > 3 months; postdated checks are not cash.

questions.questionText: A Cash Over and Short account
options: Is debited when the petty cash fund proves out over.
Is debited when the petty cash fund proves out short.
Is a contra account to cash.
questions.correctAnswer: Is debited when the petty cash fund proves out short.
questions.explanation: Cash short = debit Cash Over & Short (expense). Cash over = credit (misc. revenue).

questions.questionText: In preparing its May 31, 2007 bank reconciliation, Dogg Co. has the following information available: Balance per bank statement, 5/31/07 …………………….    Birr 30,000 Deposit in transit, 5/31/07……………………………………..        5,400 Outstanding checks, 5/31/07…………………………………         4,900 Note collected by bank in May ……………………………..          1,250 The correct balance of cash at May 31, 2007 is
questions.explanation: Bank balance 30,000 + deposit in transit 5,400 − outstanding checks 4,900 = 30,500. Books balance adjustment: + note collected 1,250 → correct cash 31,750.

questions.questionText: The category "trade receivables" includes
options: Claims against insurance companies for casualties sustained.
questions.explanation: Trade receivables = amounts owed by customers from normal credit sales. Others are non-trade receivables.

questions.questionText: When preparing bank reconciliation, bank credits are
options: Added to the bank statement balance.
Deducted from the bank statement balance.
Added to the balance per books.
Deducted from the balance per books.
questions.correctAnswer: Added to the balance per books.
questions.explanation: Bank credits (e.g. note collected, interest) not yet recorded on books → add to book balance.

questions.questionText: The journal entries for bank reconciliation
options: are taken from the "balance per bank" section only.
may include a debit to Office Expense for bank service charges.
may include a credit to Accounts Receivable for an NSF check.
may include a debit to Accounts Payable for an NSF check.
questions.correctAnswer: may include a debit to Office Expense for bank service charges.
questions.explanation: Bank service charges = expense → debit expense, credit cash (books adjustment).

questions.questionText: A deposit made by a company will appear on the bank statement as a
questions.explanation: Bank increases depositor's account → credit on bank statement.

questions.questionText: A bank statement
options: let’s a depositor know the financial position of the bank as of a certain date
is a credit reference letter written by the depositor’s bank
is a bill from the bank for services rendered
shows the activity that increased or decreased the depositor’s account balance
questions.correctAnswer: shows the activity that increased or decreased the depositor’s account balance
questions.explanation: Bank statement reports transactions affecting the depositor's account during the period.

questions.questionText: Control over cash disbursements is generally more effective when
options: all bills are paid in cash
disbursements are made by the accounts payable subsidiary clerk
all purchases are made on credit
questions.explanation: Cheques provide audit trail, authorization, and bank cancellation proof. Cash lacks these controls.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would be added to the balance per books on bank reconciliation?
questions.explanation: Bank collected note (credit on statement) not yet recorded on books → add to book balance.

questions.questionText: A bank reconciliation should be prepared
options: whenever the bank refuses to lend the company money
when an employee is suspected of fraud
to explain any difference between the depositor's balance per books with the balance per bank
by the person who is authorised to sign cheques
questions.correctAnswer: to explain any difference between the depositor's balance per books with the balance per bank
questions.explanation: Primary purpose = identify timing differences, errors, unrecorded items and ensure correct cash balance.

questions.questionText: If a cheque correctly written and paid by the bank for $438 is incorrectly recorded on the company's books for $483, the appropriate treatment on the bank reconciliation would be to
questions.explanation: Books understated cash by 45 (recorded 483 instead of 438) → add 45 to book balance to correct.

questions.questionText: Accounts receivable includes
options: amounts owed by customers on account
questions.correctAnswer: amounts owed by customers on account
questions.explanation: Accounts receivable (trade) = credit sales to customers. Others are classified separately (notes, loans, interest, advances).

questions.questionText: A written promise to pay a sum of money on demand or at a definite time is:
questions.explanation: Note receivable = formal written promise to pay (promissory note).

questions.questionText: What is the maturity value of a 90-day, 12% note of Br. 10,000?
questions.explanation: Interest = 10,000 × 0.12 × (90/360) = 300. Maturity value = principal + interest = 10,300.

questions.questionText: When a Note Receivable is discounted, Accounts Receivable is debited for what amount?
options: The face value of the note
The maturity value of the note
The maturity value of the note less accrued interest
The maturity value of the note plus accrued interest
questions.correctAnswer: The maturity value of the note
questions.explanation: When bank discounts note, contingent liability created → debit Accounts Receivable for full maturity value (if dishonored, receivable reinstated).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following items would not be considered cash?
questions.explanation: Post-dated cheque is not cash until date arrives (not currently available).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a suggested procedure to establish internal control over cash disbursements?
options: Different individuals approve and make the payments
Blank cheques are stored with limited access
The bank statement is reconciled monthly
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties requires not everyone can sign cheques — usually limited to authorized signatories.

questions.questionText: The primary source of revenue for a wholesaler is:
options: The sale of fixed assets the company
questions.explanation: Wholesaler buys goods in bulk and resells to retailers → main revenue from merchandise sales.

questions.questionText: When the terms are FOB Destination, transportation costs are covered by:
questions.explanation: FOB destination = title passes at buyer's location → seller bears shipping cost and risk in transit.

questions.questionText: In credit term “1/15, n/40”; the 15 indicates
questions.explanation: 1/15 = 1% discount if paid within 15 days; n/40 = full amount due in 40 days.

questions.questionText: Shalom enterprise earned revenue from service performed for $58,000 on credit. The effect of this transaction result in;
questions.explanation: Service on account → debit Accounts Receivable, credit Service Revenue → revenue increases.

questions.questionText: A trial balance will not balance if:
options: A correct journal entry is posted twice.
The purchase of supplies on account is debited to Supplies and credited to Cash.
A $ 550 cash drawing is debited to withdrawal for $5,500 and credited to Cash for $ 550.
A $860 payment on account is debited to Accounts Payable for $86 and credited to Cash $86.
questions.correctAnswer: A $ 550 cash drawing is debited to withdrawal for $5,500 and credited to Cash for $ 550.
questions.explanation: Debit 5,500 instead of 550 → debits exceed credits by 4,950 → trial balance out of balance.

questions.questionText: Alemu Garment paid 19,000 to creditors on account. The effect of this event in this enterprise result in;
questions.explanation: Payment to creditor → debit Accounts Payable (decrease liability), credit Cash (decrease asset).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement about adjustment is correct?
options: The adjusting entry for unearned revenues results in a decrease (a debit) to a liability account and an increase (a credit) to a revenue account.
When companies record payments of expenses that will benefit t more than one accounting period, they record an asset called prepaid expenses or prepayments.
When companies receive cash before services are performed, they have a performance obligation (liability or unearned revenue) to transfer a service to one of its customers.
Accrued revenues may accumulate (accrue) and may be unrecorded because only a portion of the total service has been provided and the clients won’t be billed until the service has been completed.
questions.explanation: All four statements accurately describe common adjusting entry situations.

exams.examName: Fundamental Accounting II Model Exam – Hawassa University

questions.questionText: A separate account or record is maintained for both cost of goods sold and merchandise inventory on hand under:
questions.explanation: In the perpetual system, inventory and cost of goods sold are updated continuously with every purchase and sale transaction — a separate running record is kept for both.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about cost of goods sold?
options: A. CGS = Cost of goods available for sale plus ending inventories
B. CGS = Cost of goods available for sale minus ending inventories
C. CGS = Cost of goods available for sale minus beginning inventories
D. CGS = Cost of goods available for sale minus cost of goods sold
questions.correctAnswer: B. CGS = Cost of goods available for sale minus ending inventories
questions.explanation: Basic inventory formula: Beginning + Purchases = Goods available for sale → Goods available – Ending inventory = Cost of goods sold.

questions.questionText: The credit terms offered to a customer by a business firm are 4/15, n/60, which means that
options: A. Four sales returns can be made within 15 days of the invoice date and no returns thereafter
B. The customer can deduct a 4% discount if the bill is paid between the 15th and 60th day from the invoice date
C. The customer can deduct a 4% discount if the bill is paid within 15 days of the invoice date
D. The customer must pay the bill within 15 days.
questions.correctAnswer: C. The customer can deduct a 4% discount if the bill is paid within 15 days of the invoice date
questions.explanation: Standard credit term notation: discount % / discount period, net / full payment due. 4/15, n/60 = 4% discount if paid within 15 days, otherwise full amount due in 60 days.

questions.questionText: The total of cost of goods or merchandise inventory on hand at the beginning of the accounting period and total cost of goods purchased during the period determine;
options: A. Cost of goods sold during the period
B. Total cost of goods purchased
C. Cost of goods available for Sale
D. Cost of ending merchandise inventory
questions.correctAnswer: C. Cost of goods available for Sale
questions.explanation: Beginning inventory + Net purchases = Cost of goods available for sale.

questions.questionText: Under the perpetual inventory method, when a firm purchases goods on credit the journal entry will include a debit to:
questions.explanation: Perpetual system directly increases the Inventory asset account (debit Inventory, credit Accounts Payable).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is/are correct about inventory error on the current period’s statements?
options: A. Overstate beginning inventory → Overstated CGS → Overstate net income
B. Understate ending inventory → understated CGS → Understated net income
C. Understate beginning inventory → Understated CGS → Overstated net income
D. Overstate ending inventory → overstated CGS → Overstated net income
questions.correctAnswer: B. Understate ending inventory → understated CGS → Understated net income
questions.explanation: Ending inventory is subtracted in CGS calculation. Understating ending inventory increases CGS → decreases gross profit & net income.

questions.questionText: Journal entry for Purchase of 900 units at Br6 per unit on account under perpetual inventory system:
questions.explanation: 900 × 6 = 5,400. Perpetual system debits Inventory directly (not Purchases account).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is /are False?
options: A. The average cost method, sometimes called the weighted average method.
B. Inventories are asset items held for sale in the ordinary course of business or goods to be used in the production of goods to be sold.
C. The FIFO method assumes that the latest goods purchased are the first to be sold
D. Perpetual inventory systems, where updates are made as seen fit.
questions.correctAnswer: C. The FIFO method assumes that the latest goods purchased are the first to be sold
questions.explanation: FIFO = First-In, First-Out → oldest goods are assumed sold first (not latest). Statement C is false.

questions.questionText: If the inventory at the end of the year is understated by $7,500, the error will cause an:
options: A. Understatement of cost of merchandise sold for the year by $7,500.
B. Overstatement of net income for the year by $7,500.
C. Overstatement of merchandise inventory for the year by $7,500.
D. Understatement of net income for the year by $7,500.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Understatement of net income for the year by $7,500.
questions.explanation: Understated ending inventory → overstated COGS → understated gross profit & net income by the same amount.

questions.questionText: Merchandise available for sale at retail is $600,000, and it is $300,000 at cost. Sales are $350,000. What is the estimated cost of the ending inventory?
From the data given above in Q-10, what is the cost retail price ratio?
questions.explanation: Cost-to-retail ratio = Cost of goods available / Retail value of goods available = 300,000 / 600,000 = 0.5 (50%).

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is a not principal feature of a periodic inventory system?
options: A. The revenues from sales are recorded when sales are made.
B. There is an attempt that can be made on the sales date to record the cost of goods sold.
C. The cost of merchandise purchases are recorded in the Purchases account.
D. It is only at the end of the fiscal period that the determination of the cost of ending inventory and goods sold are made.
questions.correctAnswer: B. There is an attempt that can be made on the sales date to record the cost of goods sold.
questions.explanation: Periodic system does NOT record COGS at the time of sale — that is a key feature of perpetual system.

questions.questionText: In the where the title or ownership to the goods passes to the buyer at the point of origin and the buyer is responsible to cover the transportation costs is known as:
questions.explanation: FOB Shipping Point = title passes at seller’s location → buyer pays freight and bears risk in transit.

questions.questionText: Yirgalem Electronics ... merchandise 90,000 FOB Shipping Point + transportation 15,000 ... Beg. Inv. 30,000 ... End. Inv. 35,000. Cost of goods sold = ?
Using FIFO (periodic) – what is cost of goods sold? (data: Beg 20@78, May 15@80, Jul 20@84, Oct 15@82, End 25 units)
questions.explanation: Total units sold = 70 – 25 = 45. FIFO → sell oldest first: 20@78 = 1,560 + 15@80 = 1,200 + 10@84 = 840 → Total COGS = 3,600.

questions.questionText: Using weighted-average (periodic) – what is cost of ending inventory?
Ending inventory understated by $15,000. Reported COGS = 80,000. Correct COGS = ?
questions.explanation: Understated ending inventory → overstated COGS by 15,000 → correct COGS = 80,000 + 15,000 = 95,000.

questions.questionText: From Q17 – reported net income 40,000. Correct net income = ?
questions.explanation: Overstated COGS by 15,000 → understated net income by 15,000 → correct NI = 40,000 – 15,000 = 25,000. (Note: many versions show 25,000; check original options carefully.)

questions.questionText: Inventory cost $3,500, selling price $5,000, completion $900, selling costs $850. Net realizable value = ?
questions.explanation: NRV = Estimated selling price – completion costs – selling costs = 5,000 – 900 – 850 = 3,250.

questions.questionText: Which inventory cost flow assumption results in higher inventory turnover ratio in an inflationary economy?
questions.explanation: In inflation, LIFO gives highest COGS → lowest ending inventory → highest turnover ratio (COGS / Avg. Inventory).

questions.questionText: Machine cost 100,000, salvage 20,000, life 5 years, straight-line. Accumulated dep. Dec 31, 2009?
Which statement is incorrect about subsequent expenditures?
options: A. Capital expenditures improve the operating efficiency of an asset.
B. Revenue expenditures are debited to an expense account.
C. Capital expenditures are debited to an asset account.
D. Subsequent expenditures are usually debited to repairs and maintenance expense account.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Subsequent expenditures are usually debited to repairs and maintenance expense account.
questions.explanation: Not all subsequent expenditures are revenue/expense — major improvements (capital) are added to asset cost.

questions.questionText: Equipment cost 120,000, accum. dep. 115,000 discarded. Result?
questions.explanation: Book value = 120,000 – 115,000 = 5,000. Discarded (assume $0 proceeds) → gain on disposal = 0 – 5,000? Wait — actually loss of 5,000 if no proceeds. (Many exams consider residual value or scrap — check context; common answer is loss 5,000.)

questions.questionText: Additions and improvements to plant assets are:
options: C. Debited to the Purchases account.
D. Debited to Plant asset account
questions.correctAnswer: D. Debited to Plant asset account
questions.explanation: Capital improvements that extend life or increase capacity/value are capitalized (debited to asset).

questions.questionText: Building dep. expense 20,000 (2010), 20-year life, residual 20,000, straight-line. Original cost?
Equipment 80,000, 6 years, salvage 8,000, straight-line. Original annual depreciation?
Beginning of year 4: revised life 11 years total, salvage 4,000. Revised annual dep. expense?
questions.explanation: After 3 years dep. = 3 × 12,000 = 36,000. Book value = 80,000 – 36,000 = 44,000. Remaining life = 8 years (11 – 3), new salvage 4,000. Revised dep. = (44,000 – 4,000) / 8 = 40,000 / 8 = 5,000. (Note: many exams show different rounding or interpretation — check exact wording.)

questions.questionText: The process of transferring the cost of natural resources to an expense account is called____?
questions.explanation: Depletion is used for wasting assets (mines, oil, timber, etc.).

questions.questionText: Equipment cash price 24,000 + custom duty 1,200 + insurance transit 200 + installation 400. Total cost?
questions.explanation: All costs necessary to get asset ready for use are capitalized: 24,000 + 1,200 + 200 + 400 = 25,800.

questions.questionText: Machine €80,000, 10-year life, no residual, straight-line, sold June 30, 2017 for €26,000 after purchase Jan 1, 2013. Gain/loss?
questions.explanation: Annual dep. = 80,000 / 10 = 8,000. 4.5 years dep. = 36,000. Book value = 80,000 – 36,000 = 44,000. Sold 26,000 → loss = 44,000 – 26,000 = 18,000. (Check half-year convention — many exams use 4 years or different calculation.)

questions.questionText: What is the amount of depreciation expense, using declining-balance method for the second year of use for machine initial cost $24,000 with residual value of $2,000 and useful life of five years?
questions.explanation: Declining balance rate = 2/5 = 40%. Year 1 dep = 24,000 × 40% = 9,600. Book value end year 1 = 24,000 – 9,600 = 14,400. Year 2 dep = 14,400 × 40% = 5,760.

questions.questionText: When there is a change in estimated depreciation:
options: A. Previous depreciation should be corrected.
B. Current and future years’ depreciation should be revised.
C. Only future years’ depreciation should be revised.
D. It is an accounting error
questions.correctAnswer: B. Current and future years’ depreciation should be revised.
questions.explanation: Change in estimate (useful life, salvage value) is prospective — adjust current and remaining periods; no retroactive correction.

questions.questionText: BB expects to extract 20 million tons of coal from a mine that cost ETB 12 million. If no residual value is expected and 2 million tons are mined in the first year, the entry to record depletion will include a:
options: A. Debit to accumulated depletion of ETB 2,000,000.
B. Debit to depletion expense of ETB 1,200,000.
C. Credit to natural resource of ETB 1,200,000.
D. Credit to accumulated depletion of ETB 2,000,000.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Debit to depletion expense of ETB 1,200,000.
questions.explanation: Depletion rate = 12,000,000 / 20,000,000 = 0.60 per ton. Year 1 = 2,000,000 tons × 0.60 = 1,200,000 → Debit Depletion Expense, Credit Accumulated Depletion.

questions.questionText: LCD Corporation purchased a patent for $180,000 on September 1, 2006. It had a useful life of 10 years. On January 1, 2008, spent $44,000 to successfully defend the patent in a lawsuit. Remaining useful life is 5 years as of that date. Patent amortization expense for 2008?
questions.explanation: Original book value Jan 1, 2008: 180,000 – (180,000/10 × 16/12) ≈ 180,000 – 24,000 = 156,000. Add defense cost 44,000 → new BV 200,000. Remaining life 5 years → 200,000 / 5 = 40,000 per year. But many exams use full-year convention or slight variation; standard answer often ≈37,600–40,000 range.

questions.questionText: A company purchased land to be used as the site for the construction of a plant. Timber was cut from the building site so that construction of the plant could begin. The proceeds from the sale of the timber should be
options: B. Netted against the costs to clear the land and expensed as incurred.
C. Deducted from the cost of the plant.
D. Deducted from the cost of the land.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Deducted from the cost of the land.
questions.explanation: Proceeds from timber sale reduce the capitalized cost of the land (preparation costs net of recoveries).

questions.questionText: Depreciation is a systematic and rational technique of:
questions.explanation: Depreciation allocates the cost of a tangible fixed asset over its useful life — it is a cost allocation process, not valuation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is among the characteristics of plant, property & equipment?
options: A. Held for sale in the normal course of business
D. Held for use in operations
questions.correctAnswer: D. Held for use in operations
questions.explanation: PPE (fixed assets) are tangible assets held for use in production/supply of goods/services or rental/administrative purposes (not for sale).

questions.questionText: The rights, privileges, and competitive advantages that result from the ownership of long-lived assets that do not possess physical substance are:
questions.explanation: Definition of intangible assets (patents, copyrights, trademarks, goodwill, etc.).

questions.questionText: Which cost is not included as part of the cost of a land?
options: D. Cost of structural additions made to the land with definite life.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Cost of structural additions made to the land with definite life.
questions.explanation: Buildings and other structures with limited life are capitalized separately (not to land cost).

questions.questionText: Disposal of a plant, property and equipment involves
questions.explanation: To remove the asset from books: Debit Accum. Dep. + Debit Cash/Proceeds + Debit Loss (or Credit Gain) + Credit Asset account.

questions.questionText: Gross profit will result if:
options: A. Operating expenses are less than net income.
B. Sales revenues are greater than operating expenses.
C. Sales revenues are greater than cost of goods sold.
D. Operating expenses are greater than cost of goods sold.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Sales revenues are greater than cost of goods sold.
questions.explanation: Gross profit = Sales – Cost of Goods Sold.

questions.questionText: Under a perpetual inventory system, when goods are purchased for resale by a company:
options: A. Purchases account are debited to Merchandise Inventory.
B. Purchases on account are debited to Purchases.
C. Purchase returns are debited to Purchase Returns and Allowances.
D. Freight costs are debited to Freight-out
questions.correctAnswer: A. Purchases account are debited to Merchandise Inventory.
questions.explanation: Perpetual system: debit Inventory (not Purchases) for acquisitions.

questions.questionText: The sales accounts that normally have a debit balance are:
questions.explanation: Sales Discounts and Sales Returns & Allowances are contra-revenue accounts with normal debit balances.

questions.questionText: A credit sale of $750 is made on June 13, terms 2/10, net/30. A return of $50 is granted on June 16. The amount received as payment in full on June 23 is:
questions.explanation: Net invoice = 750 – 50 = 700. 2% discount if within 10 days → 700 × 0.98 = 686.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accounts will normally appear in the ledger of a merchandising company that uses a perpetual inventory system?
questions.explanation: Perpetual system uses COGS account (updated at each sale); periodic uses Purchases.

questions.questionText: To record the sale of goods for cash in a perpetual inventory system:
options: A. Only one journal entry is necessary to record cost of goods sold and reduction of inventory.
B. Only one journal entry is necessary to record the receipt of cash and the sales revenue.
C. Two journal entries are necessary: one to record the receipt of cash and sales revenue, and one to record the cost of goods sold and reduction of inventory.
D. Two journal entries are necessary: one to record the receipt of cash and reduction of inventory, and one to record the cost of goods sold and sales revenue
questions.correctAnswer: C. Two journal entries are necessary...
questions.explanation: Perpetual: (1) Dr Cash / Cr Sales, (2) Dr COGS / Cr Inventory.

questions.questionText: The steps in the accounting cycle for a merchandising company are the same as those in a service company except:
options: A. An additional adjusting journal entry for inventory may be needed in a merchandising company.
B. Closing journal entries are not required for a merchandising company.
C. A post-closing trial balance is not required for a merchandising company.
D. A multiple-step income statement is required for a merchandising company
questions.correctAnswer: A. An additional adjusting journal entry for inventory may be needed in a merchandising company.
questions.explanation: Periodic system needs year-end adjustment to update inventory & COGS; perpetual usually does not.

questions.questionText: The multiple-step income statement for a merchandising company shows each of the following features except:
questions.explanation: Investing activities appear in the statement of cash flows, not income statement.

questions.questionText: When goods are purchased for resale by a company using a periodic inventory system:
options: A. Purchases on account are debited to Merchandise Inventory.
B. Purchases on account are debited to Purchases.
C. Purchase returns are debited to Purchase Returns and Allowances.
D. Freight costs are debited to Purchases
questions.correctAnswer: B. Purchases on account are debited to Purchases.
questions.explanation: Periodic system uses Purchases account (not Inventory).

questions.questionText: In determining cost of goods sold:
options: A. Purchase discounts are deducted from net purchases.
B. Freight-out is added to net purchases.
C. Purchase returns and allowances are deducted from net purchases.
D. Freight-in is added to net purchases
questions.correctAnswer: D. Freight-in is added to net purchases
questions.explanation: Net purchases = Purchases – Returns – Discounts + Freight-in.

questions.questionText: A company has cash sales of $75,000, credit sales of $320,000, sales returns and allowances of $13,700, and sales discounts of $6,000. Its net sales equal
questions.explanation: Gross sales = 75,000 + 320,000 = 395,000. Net sales = Gross sales – Returns & Allowances – Discounts = 395,000 – 13,700 – 6,000 = 375,300.

questions.questionText: If merchandise purchased on account is returned, the buyer may inform the seller of the details by issuing
questions.explanation: The buyer issues a debit memorandum to reduce (debit) Accounts Payable when returning goods or claiming an allowance.

questions.questionText: The income statement in which the total of all expenses is deducted from the total of all revenues is termed:
questions.explanation: Single-step income statement simply subtracts total expenses from total revenues to get net income (no gross profit subtotal).

questions.questionText: Which of the following expenses would normally be classified as other expense on a multiple-step income statement?
questions.explanation: Interest expense is usually shown in the 'other expenses and losses' section after operating income (not part of operating expenses).

questions.questionText: A kind of inventory system which updates accounting records for each purchase and each sale of inventory is
options: B. Just in time inventory system
questions.explanation: Perpetual system continuously updates Inventory and COGS with every transaction.

questions.questionText: ____________ refers to a seller granting a price reduction (allowance) to a buyer of defective or unacceptable merchandise.
questions.explanation: Purchase allowance is a reduction in price for defective/damaged goods without returning them.

questions.questionText: In FOB shipping point agreement, which of the following is true:
options: A. ownership of goods transfers to the buyer when the goods arrive at the buyer’s place of business
B. The buyer accepts ownership when the goods depart the seller’s place of business
C. The seller pays shipping costs and has the risk of loss in transit
D. The goods are part of the seller’s inventory when they are in transit
questions.correctAnswer: B. The buyer accepts ownership when the goods depart the seller’s place of business
questions.explanation: FOB Shipping Point: title passes at seller's location → buyer owns goods in transit and pays freight.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is true about expenses incurred by merchandising business
options: A. Selling expenses are the expenses of advertising merchandise, making sales, and delivering goods to customers.
B. General and administrative expenses support a company’s overall operations and include expenses related to accounting, human resources, and finance
C. Other expenses and losses commonly do not include interest expense, losses from asset disposals, and casualty losses
D. Operating expenses are separated into two parts selling and General and Administrative expense.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Operating expenses are separated into two parts selling and General and Administrative expense.
questions.explanation: In multiple-step income statements, operating expenses are classified into selling expenses and general & administrative expenses.

questions.questionText: In a partnership of Sun and Star, net income Br.50,000. Sharing ratio 40:60 after salary allowances 15,000 and 10,000. Net income share to Star?
questions.explanation: Remaining profit after salaries = 50,000 – 15,000 – 10,000 = 25,000. Star gets 60% = 15,000. Total for Star = 15,000 + 10,000 = 25,000. (Note: many similar questions show slight variation; check exact wording for correct total.)

questions.questionText: When a new partner is admitted by contributing assets to a partnership
options: A. Both the assets and the owners’ equity of the firm are not been affected
B. The liabilities of the partnership are decreased
C. Both the assets and the owner equity of the firm are increased
D. Assets of the partnership increased but the owners’ equity of the firm will not be affected
questions.correctAnswer: C. Both the assets and the owner equity of the firm are increased
questions.explanation: New partner's investment increases assets (cash/assets contributed) and increases total partners' equity (new capital account).

questions.questionText: Disadvantages of the partnership form of business organization, compared to corporations, include:
options: A. Many legal requirements to form.
B. The partnership pays income taxes.
C. Unlimited liability for the partners.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Unlimited liability for the partners.
questions.explanation: Partners have unlimited personal liability for partnership debts (unlike corporations' limited liability).

questions.questionText: Delu and Mulu capital 90,000 each, ratio 4:6. Yohannes admitted with 40% interest for Br 100,000 cash. Capital balance of Yohannes after admission?
questions.explanation: Total capital before = 180,000 + 100,000 = 280,000. Yohannes 40% = 280,000 × 40% = 112,000 (but many use bonus/goodwill method; direct investment often records at contributed amount or adjusted).

questions.questionText: Referring to previous question, capital balance of Delu immediately after admission?
questions.explanation: In bonus method or direct investment without revaluation, old partners' capitals usually remain unchanged unless goodwill/bonus is recognized.

questions.questionText: When a partner withdraws from the partnership by taking assets, the effects or entry result in:
options: A. Increase the assets of the partnership
B. Increase to the asset and owner’s equity of the firm
C. Decrease to the asset and owner’s equity of the firm
D. Change for the liability of the firm
questions.correctAnswer: C. Decrease to the asset and owner’s equity of the firm
questions.explanation: Withdrawal reduces partnership assets (cash/assets paid out) and reduces the withdrawing partner's capital (equity).

questions.questionText: In partnership liquidation, balance sheet shows capitals D 21,000, E 50,000, H 37,000; liability 8,500. After settlement, capitals D (2,000 Dr), E 18,000 Cr, H 21,000 Cr. Gain or loss on realization?
questions.explanation: Total capital before = 108,000 – liability 8,500 = net assets 99,500. Final capitals sum = –2,000 + 18,000 + 21,000 = 37,000. Realization loss = 99,500 – 37,000 = 62,500 (check exact arithmetic in original).

questions.questionText: In the partnership of T, L and A, they decided to terminate the business. During liquidating the partnership the assets sold at a loss and, L, one of the partners shared of loss over the balance of his capital account. Moreover, L was not able to pay the entire deficiency. How were the claims among the partners settled with regard to deficiency?
options: A. The deficiency is shared for all partners.
B. Deficiency is reduced from partnership assets.
C. The remaining partners share the deficiency.
D. Ignore the deficiency and wind up the firm.
questions.correctAnswer: C. The remaining partners share the deficiency.
questions.explanation: When a partner has a capital deficiency and cannot pay it (insolvent), the loss from the deficiency is absorbed by the remaining solvent partners in their profit/loss sharing ratio.

questions.questionText: In a partnership of A and B, they reported net income of 70,000 for the year ended 2019. The partners agreed net income sharing ratio was 30% and 45%, respectively. What is the amount of net income share to B?
questions.explanation: The percentages appear incomplete (do not add to 100%). Assuming the ratio is 30:45 and remainder is implicit or typo, many similar questions treat it as 30:70 or adjust — but standard calculation if 30:45 of total profit → B gets 45/75 × 70,000 ≈ 42,000. Check original for exact ratio wording.

questions.questionText: In a partnership of F and N, net income 50,000 Br. Sharing ratio 30% and 45%, salary allowance 15,000 and 10,000. Net income share to F?
questions.explanation: Profit after salaries = 50,000 – 15,000 – 10,000 = 25,000. Remaining shared 30:45 (or 2:3). F gets 2/5 × 25,000 = 10,000 + salary 15,000 = 25,000. (Common variation shows 20,000–25,000 depending on ratio interpretation.)

questions.questionText: Beshir contributed $8,000 cash and truck (cost $35,000, accum. dep. $15,000, fair value $16,000). Sadam contributed garage (cost $40,000, fair value $55,000). Combined total capital recorded?
questions.explanation: Partnership records contributed assets at **fair value**: Cash 8,000 + Truck 16,000 + Garage 55,000 = 79,000. (Some questions use book value — but standard is fair value → check context; many exams use 8k + 16k + 55k = 79k.)

questions.questionText: A type of partnership which is a business organization consisting of partners who are each jointly and severally liable with the partnership itself for the obligations of the partnership.
questions.explanation: In a general partnership, all partners have unlimited joint and several liability.

questions.questionText: The income statement for a partnership is identical to the income statement for a corporation except
options: A. For the capital section of the income statement
B. For the additional section that reports the division of net income
C. For the withdrawal section of each partner
D. For the additional investment section of the partnership
questions.correctAnswer: B. For the additional section that reports the division of net income
questions.explanation: Partnership income statement usually shows net income, then includes a schedule/statement showing allocation to partners (salaries, interest, remainder).

questions.questionText: The legal characteristic of a partnership whereby each partner is an agent of the partnership and is able to bind the partnership to contracts within the normal scope of the partnership business is known as:
questions.explanation: Mutual agency means any partner can enter into contracts that bind the partnership.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true regarding a partnership?
options: B. Partnership is a voluntary association
questions.explanation: Partnerships are pass-through entities — they do not pay income tax; income is taxed at the partner level.

questions.questionText: A and B share profits and losses 2:1 after salary allowance 12,000 to B. Earnings 39,000. Amount credited to Capital account of A?
questions.explanation: After salary to B: 39,000 – 12,000 = 27,000 remaining. A gets 2/3 × 27,000 = 18,000. (Some include interest — but here only salary; check exact for salary impact on A.)

questions.questionText: The dissolution of a partnership occurs
options: A. Only when the partnership sells its assets and permanently closes its books.
B. Only when a partner leaves the partnership.
C. At the end of each year, when income is allocated to the partners.
D. Only when a new partner is admitted to the partnership
E. when there is any change in the individuals who make up the partnership
questions.correctAnswer: E. when there is any change in the individuals who make up the partnership
questions.explanation: Technically, dissolution occurs upon any change in partners (admission, withdrawal, death), though business may continue as reconstitution.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT an essential feature of a partnership?
options: A. There must be a business.
B. The business must be carried on for profits.
C. The business must be carried on by all the partners.
D. There must be an agreement.
questions.correctAnswer: C. The business must be carried on by all the partners.
questions.explanation: Partners do not all have to actively manage — some can be dormant/sleeping partners.

questions.questionText: When a Goodwill Account is raised, the credit is given to the old partner’s capital account in _____
options: D. None of the options are correct.
questions.explanation: Goodwill raised on admission/reconstitution is credited to old partners in their old ratio.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum partner requirement to start a partnership firm?
questions.explanation: Minimum of 2 partners required to form a partnership (maximum varies by country — often 20 for general, unlimited for banking).

questions.questionText: What is the liability of partners in a partnership firm?
options: C. Limited to the capital of business
questions.explanation: In general partnerships, liability is unlimited and joint & several.

questions.questionText: How will the profits be divided among partners in the absence of a partnership deed?
options: A. Depending on the capital invested.
B. Depending on the work experience.
questions.explanation: In absence of agreement, profits and losses are shared equally regardless of capital contribution.

questions.questionText: Akhil and Ravi are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 7:3 with capitals of birr 800,000 and birr 600,000 respectively. According to partnership deed interest on capital is to be provided @ 8% p.a. and is to be treated as a charge. Profit for the year is birr 80,000. Choose the correct option:
options: A. A will be credited by birr 64,000 and B will be credited by birr 48,000.
B. A will be credited by birr 56,000 and B will be credited by birr 24,000.
C. A will be credited by birr 22,400 and B will be credited by birr 9,600.
D. A will be credited by birr 41,600 and B will be credited by birr 38,400.
questions.correctAnswer: B. A will be credited by birr 56,000 and B will be credited by birr 24,000.
questions.explanation: Interest on capital (charge against profit): A 800,000 × 8% = 64,000; Ravi 600,000 × 8% = 48,000. Total interest 112,000 > profit 80,000 → interest is limited to profit and shared in ratio 7:3 → A: 56,000, Ravi: 24,000.

questions.questionText: At the time of admission of a partner, who decides the share of profit of the new partner out of the firm’s profit?
questions.explanation: Old partners collectively decide the new partner's profit share (via agreement).

questions.questionText: P and Q are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:1 with capitals birr 100,000 and birr 80,000 respectively. The interest on capital has been provided to them @ 8% instead of 10%. In the rectifying adjustment entry, Q will be:
questions.explanation: Short interest to Q: 80,000 × (10% – 8%) = 1,600 short total, but per partner adjustment needed — Q gets credit for under-provided interest.

questions.questionText: The relation of partner with the firm is that of:
options: C. An owner and agent both
questions.correctAnswer: C. An owner and agent both
questions.explanation: Partners are co-owners and agents of the firm (mutual agency principle).

questions.questionText: A and B are partners sharing profits and losses equally. They admitted C as a partner with an equal share giving him a guarantee of minimum birr 50,000 profit p.a. The profit for the year after C’s admission was birr120,000. What will be the net amount that will be credited to A’s Capital A/c?
questions.explanation: Profit 120,000 ÷ 3 = 40,000 each. C gets minimum 50,000 → deficiency 10,000 borne by A & B equally → A gets 40,000 – 5,000 = 35,000 (wait — common answer 40,000 if guarantee adjustment differs).

questions.questionText: X and Y are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2 with capitals birr 500,000 each. According to partnership deed, interest on capital is allowed @ 10%.The profit for the year is birr 50,000. What amount will be credited to X and Y in such condition?
options: A. birr 50,000 to A and B each
B. birr 25,000 to A and B each
C. birr 30,000 to A and birr 20,000 to B
questions.explanation: Interest = 500,000 × 10% × 2 = 100,000 > profit 50,000 → interest abated and shared in ratio 3:2 → X 30,000, Y 20,000 (option C is close but wording 'to A and B' confuses).

questions.questionText: A, B and C are partner’s in a firm. If D is admitted as a new partner:
options: B. old firm and old partnership is dissolved
questions.explanation: Admission reconstitutes the partnership (new agreement), but firm may continue.

questions.questionText: In partnership accounting, goodwill raised at the time of retirement of a partner is credited to:
questions.explanation: Goodwill adjustment on retirement benefits retiring partner; credited to remaining partners' capitals.

questions.questionText: When a partner retires, the retiring partner's share of profit/loss on revaluation is transferred to:
questions.explanation: Revaluation profit/loss share goes to retiring partner's capital before final settlement.

questions.questionText: In partnership dissolution, if a partner becomes insolvent and cannot pay deficiency, it is borne by:
options: B. Remaining solvent partners in profit-sharing ratio
questions.correctAnswer: B. Remaining solvent partners in profit-sharing ratio
questions.explanation: Garner vs Murray rule: deficiency of insolvent partner borne by solvent partners in P/L ratio.

questions.questionText: The maximum number of partners in a banking partnership firm in Ethiopia is:
questions.explanation: Per Ethiopian law (Commercial Code), banking partnerships limited to 10 partners.

questions.questionText: When goodwill is not recorded in books on admission of a partner, the adjustment is made through:
questions.explanation: Hidden goodwill or premium method adjusts via partners' capital accounts.

questions.questionText: In piecemeal distribution during partnership liquidation, cash is distributed first to:
questions.explanation: Priority: outside creditors > partner loans > partner capitals.

questions.questionText: A partner acts as an agent of:
options: B. The firm and other partners
questions.correctAnswer: B. The firm and other partners
questions.explanation: Mutual agency principle.

questions.questionText: If there is no partnership deed, interest on partner's loan to firm is allowed at:
questions.explanation: Default rate in absence of agreement (common in many jurisdictions; Ethiopian law aligns similarly).

questions.questionText: On dissolution, partner's loan is treated as:
questions.explanation: Partner loans rank above capital in payment priority.

questions.questionText: The account used to close all nominal accounts in partnership is:
questions.explanation: Appropriation account divides net profit per deed.

questions.questionText: When a partner is admitted, sacrificing ratio is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Sacrifice = old share – new share for each old partner.

questions.questionText: In case of retirement, the gaining ratio is:
questions.explanation: Gain to continuing partners = new share – old share.

questions.questionText: The final account prepared in partnership dissolution is:
questions.explanation: Cash/Bank account shows final distribution after realisation and payment of liabilities.

exams.examName: Intermediate Financial Accounting - I Model Exam @ 2016

questions.questionText: When the rules in IFRS or IAS standard are contrary to what the framework says:
options: We need to develop our own accounting policy
questions.explanation: Specific IFRS/IAS standards take precedence over the Conceptual Framework when there is a conflict, as the Framework is not itself a standard but provides guidance for developing policies in the absence of specific rules.

questions.questionText: Income as per the IASB’s conceptual framework may represent:
options: Increases in liabilities that result in increase in equity
Decreases in liability that result in increases in equity
Decreases in economic benefits that increase equity
questions.correctAnswer: Decreases in liability that result in increases in equity
questions.explanation: Per the IASB Conceptual Framework, income includes increases in assets or decreases in liabilities that result in increases in equity (other than contributions from equity participants).

questions.questionText: At the end of the fiscal year, before the accounts are adjusted, Accounts Receivable has a balance of $200,000 and Allowance for Doubtful Accounts has a credit balance of $2,500. If the estimate of uncollectible accounts determined by aging the receivables is $8,500, the amount of bad debt expense is:
questions.explanation: Under the aging method (balance sheet approach), bad debt expense = Desired ending allowance ($8,500) – Existing credit balance ($2,500) = $6,000.

questions.questionText: Liability is
options: A present obligation resulting from future events
Results in an inflow of economic benefits to the entity.
The residual interest in the assets.
A present obligation of the entity arising from past events.
questions.correctAnswer: A present obligation of the entity arising from past events.
questions.explanation: Per the Conceptual Framework, a liability is a present obligation arising from past events, expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits.

questions.questionText: As an aim of presentation and disclosures, effective communication of information requires
options: Grouping similar items and separate dissimilar items
Providing an extremely detailed and bulky information
Providing excessively aggregated information to challenge users.
Sufficient details to disclose matters regardless of cost of preparation.
questions.correctAnswer: Grouping similar items and separate dissimilar items
questions.explanation: Effective presentation under IFRS involves classification: aggregating similar items and separating dissimilar ones for understandability (per IAS 1 and Conceptual Framework).

questions.questionText: Who are the two key organizations in the development of international accounting standards?
questions.explanation: The IASB develops IFRS, while IOSCO (International Organization of Securities Commissions) promotes and endorses their use globally.

questions.questionText: At the end of the fiscal year, Accounts Receivable has a balance of $100,000, Allowance for Doubtful Accounts has a balance of $7,000 and sales returns and discounts are $2500. The expected net realizable value of the accounts receivable is:
questions.explanation: Net realizable value = Accounts Receivable ($100,000) – Allowance ($7,000) = $93,000. (Sales returns/discounts affect gross receivables but are already reflected or separate; NRV focuses on allowance adjustment.)

questions.questionText: IFRS is comprised of:
options: International Financial Reporting Standards, International Accounting Standards, and international accounting interpretations.
International Accounting Standards and international accounting interpretations.
FASB financial reporting standards and International Accounting Standards.
