questions.explanation: Labor costs are tested in payroll cycle before allocation to inventory.

questions.questionText: For retail and wholesale businesses, the most important inventory is:
questions.explanation: Retail/wholesale primary inventory is finished goods/merchandise.

questions.questionText: In most manufacturing companies, the inventory and warehousing cycle begins with the:
options: A. Receipt of a customer’s order.
B. Completion of production of a customer’s order.
C. Initiation of production of a customer’s order.
D. Acquisition of raw materials for production of an order
questions.correctAnswer: D. Acquisition of raw materials for production of an order
questions.explanation: Cycle starts with purchase of raw materials.

questions.questionText: The audit tests to verify that the client is using an inventory method which is generally accepted and to verify that physical counts were correctly summarized are performed during the audit of the:
questions.explanation: Valuation method and count summarization are inventory cycle procedures.

questions.questionText: Almost all companies need physical controls over their assets to prevent loss. Which of the following is not an example of such a control?
options: C. Custody of assets assigned to specific responsible individuals.
D. Approved prenumbered documents for authorizing movement of inventory.
questions.explanation: Perpetual files are record-keeping, not physical control.

questions.questionText: Handling the receipt of ordered goods is a part of the ________ cycle.
questions.explanation: Receiving goods is part of acquisitions and payments cycle.

questions.questionText: There must be a periodic physical count by the client of the inventory items on hand:
options: A. Only if the client uses the LIFO method.
B. Only if the client uses a lower-of-cost-or-market method.
C. Regardless of the client’s inventory valuation method.
D. Only if the client uses either the LIFO or FIFO method.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Regardless of the client’s inventory valuation method.
questions.explanation: Physical count is required under most GAAP/IFRS methods.

questions.questionText: If the auditor concludes that physical controls over inventory are so inadequate that the inventory will be difficult to count, the auditor should ordinarily:
options: B. Issue a qualified audit report.
C. Conduct expanded observation tests of physical inventory.
D. Hire a specialist to assist the auditor.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Conduct expanded observation tests of physical inventory.
questions.explanation: Auditor expands observation procedures when controls are weak.

questions.questionText: From which of the following evidence-gathering audit procedures would an auditor obtain most assurance concerning the existence of inventories?
options: A. Observation of physical inventory counts.
B. Written inventory representations from management.
C. Confirmation of inventories in a public warehouse.
D. Auditor’s re-computation of inventory extensions.
questions.correctAnswer: A. Observation of physical inventory counts.
questions.explanation: Physical observation provides the strongest evidence for existence.

questions.questionText: Which of the following control procedures would most likely be used to maintain accurate perpetual inventory records?
options: A. Independent storeroom count of goods received.
B. Periodic independent comparison of records with goods on hand.
C. Periodic independent reconciliation of control and subsidiary records.
D. Independent matching of purchase orders, receiving reports, and vendors’ invoices.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Periodic independent comparison of records with goods on hand.
questions.explanation: Cycle counts reconcile perpetual records to physical.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a generally recognized inventory method?
questions.explanation: LOFO (Last Out First Out) is not a standard method.

questions.questionText: Auditors test the quantity of materials charged to work-in-process by tracing these quantities to:
questions.explanation: Material requisitions authorize transfer to production.

questions.questionText: After accounting for a sequence of inventory tags, an auditor traces a sample of tags to the physical inventory listing to obtain evidence that all items:
options: A. Included in the listing have been counted.
B. Represented by inventory tags actually exist.
C. Represented by inventory tags are included in the listing.
D. Included in the listing are represented by inventory tags.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Represented by inventory tags are included in the listing.
questions.explanation: Tag-to-listing trace tests completeness of listing.

questions.questionText: If the perpetual inventory master files show lower quantities of inventory than the physical count, an explanation of the difference might be unrecorded:
questions.explanation: Unrecorded receipts would cause perpetual to be lower than physical.

questions.questionText: Pricing manufactured inventory is difficult. Auditors must evaluate the method of allocating manufacturing overhead for all but which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under IFRS/older standards, focus is on consistency, reasonableness, accuracy — not strict FASB pronouncement (US GAAP).

questions.questionText: Tests of the perpetual inventory master files for the purpose of reducing the tests of physical inventory or changing their timing are done through the use of:
questions.explanation: Roll-forward/roll-back tests use documentation (receipts, shipments).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following procedures would not be appropriate for an auditor in discharging his responsibilities concerning the client’s physical inventories?
options: A. Confirmation of goods in the hands of public warehouses.
B. Supervising the taking of the annual physical inventory.
C. Carrying out physical inventory procedures at an interim date.
D. Obtaining written representation from the client as to the existence, quality, and dollar amount of the inventory.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Supervising the taking of the annual physical inventory.
questions.explanation: Auditor observes, does not supervise (management responsibility).

questions.questionText: The test of details of balance procedure which requires the auditor to account for unused inventory tag numbers to make sure none have been deleted is associated with the audit objective of:
questions.explanation: Accounting for all tags ensures no items omitted from listing.

questions.questionText: A well-designed computerized system of perpetual inventory master files includes information about the:
options: A. Units of inventory purchased, sold, and on hand.
B. Unit costs of inventory purchased, sold, and on hand.
C. Units of raw materials, work-in-process, and finished goods.
D. Units and unit costs of inventory purchased, sold, and on hand.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Units and unit costs of inventory purchased, sold, and on hand.
questions.explanation: Perpetual system tracks both quantity and cost.

questions.questionText: All of the following are accounts that fall under the acquisition and payment cycle except:
questions.explanation: AR is sales and collection cycle.

questions.questionText: An auditor can improve the efficiency and effectiveness of an audit of fixed assets by performing which of the following tests separately?
options: B. Verification of current year sale of merchandise
questions.explanation: Disposals can be tested separately from additions.

questions.questionText: To begin an audit of current year acquisitions, the auditor should request the client provide them with:
questions.explanation: Property master file lists additions and details.

questions.questionText: The most important balance-related objectives for depreciation expense is:
questions.explanation: Depreciation is primarily an accuracy/calculation assertion.

questions.questionText: An auditor should review the client's insurance policies to determine if:
options: A. The client is over-paying for insurance
B. The client has rights to the policy
D. The client has chosen the correct insurance provider
questions.explanation: Coverage adequacy and rights/assignment are key.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accounts is not part of the capital acquisition and repayment cycle?
questions.explanation: Unearned revenue is sales/collection cycle.

questions.questionText: When reviewing controls over notes payable, an auditor should determine if:
options: A. There is proper authorization for issuing of new notes
B. There are proper documents and records
C. There are adequate controls over the repayment of principle and interest
questions.explanation: All are key controls for debt cycle.

questions.questionText: The audit objective of existence for notes payable is tested by:
options: A. Footing the notes payable account
B. Tracing the notes payable to the master file
C. Examining board of directors minutes
D. Tracing totals to the General Ledger
questions.correctAnswer: C. Examining board of directors minutes
questions.explanation: Authorization in minutes supports existence of debt.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the focus of an audit of cash for most companies?
questions.explanation: Primary focus is the main operating bank account.

questions.questionText: Which of the following cycles does not affect cash in bank?
questions.explanation: Inventory cycle affects assets, not directly cash (unless purchases paid immediately).

questions.questionText: The general cash account is considered significant in almost all audits:
options: A. Where the ending balance is material.
B. Even when the ending balance is immaterial.
C. Except those of not-for-profit organizations.
D. Where either the beginning or ending balance is material
questions.correctAnswer: B. Even when the ending balance is immaterial.
questions.explanation: Cash is always audited due to high inherent risk, even if balance is small.

questions.questionText: Because cash is the most desirable asset for people to steal, it has a higher:
questions.explanation: High susceptibility to misappropriation → high inherent risk.

questions.questionText: The most important balance-related audit objectives in the audit of cash include all but which of the following?
questions.explanation: Occurrence is a transaction assertion; cash balance assertions are existence, completeness, accuracy, etc.

questions.questionText: Which of the following items would not normally appear on bank reconciliations?
options: C. List of deposits in transit
questions.explanation: Outstanding deposits is not standard terminology; deposits in transit is the correct term.

questions.questionText: The concern in a monthly proof of cash is with:
options: B. Reconciling the amounts per books and bank.
questions.explanation: Proof of cash reconciles book and bank amounts monthly to detect kiting/transfers.

questions.questionText: A lawyer's refusal to respond to a letter of audit inquiry normally requires the auditor to issue a
options: A. Unqualified opinion with an explanatory paragraph
C. Qualified opinion or a disclaimer or opinion
questions.correctAnswer: C. Qualified opinion or a disclaimer or opinion
questions.explanation: Scope limitation from non-response → qualified or disclaimer.

questions.questionText: A representation letter issued by a client
options: A. Is a substitute for testing
B. Does not reduce the auditor's responsibility
C. Reduces the auditor's responsibility only to the extent that it is relied upon
D. Is essential for the preparation of the audit program
questions.correctAnswer: B. Does not reduce the auditor's responsibility
questions.explanation: Management representations complement, but do not replace, audit evidence.

questions.questionText: Analytical procedures
options: A. Are required to be performed in the planning phase of the audit
B. Are often done during the examination's testing stage
C. Are required to be done during the completion phase of the audit
questions.explanation: Required in planning & completion; optional in substantive testing.

questions.questionText: An auditor should obtain evidential matter relevant to each of the following factors concerning third-party litigation against a client except the
options: A. Existence of a situation indicating uncertainty as to the possible loss
B. Jurisdiction in which the matter will be resolved
C. Period in which the underlying cause of legal action occurred
D. Probability of an unfavorable outcome
questions.correctAnswer: B. Jurisdiction in which the matter will be resolved
questions.explanation: Jurisdiction is less relevant to loss estimation than probability, timing, and existence.

questions.questionText: If on the basis of the additional procedures carried out and the information obtained, including the effect of mitigating circumstances, the auditor's judgment is that the entity will not be able to continue as a going concern, the financial statements should be prepared using an appropriate basis; otherwise, the auditor will issue a
options: D. Unqualified opinion with emphasis of a matter paragraph
questions.explanation: Inappropriate basis (not going concern when required) → adverse opinion.

questions.questionText: Which method of an analytical procedure is most useful because many expenses, such as the cost of goods sold, might be expected to bear a predictable relationship to net sales?
questions.explanation: Reasonableness tests compare expected vs. actual based on relationships (e.g., COGS to sales).

questions.questionText: Which of the following standards or group of standards is mostly affected by a computerized information system environment?
options: D. Second standard of field work
questions.explanation: Fieldwork standards (evidence, supervision) are most impacted by IT environment.

questions.questionText: It relates to materiality of the financial statement assertions affected by the computer processing.
questions.explanation: IT significance relates to materiality of affected assertions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the least likely characteristic of personal computers?
options: A. They are small enough to be transportable.
C. They can be placed in operation quickly.
D. The operating system software is less comprehensive than that found in larger computer environments.
questions.explanation: PCs are generally inexpensive compared to mainframes.

questions.questionText: A collection of data that is shared and used by a number of different users for different purposes.
questions.explanation: Database definition.

questions.questionText: The applications of auditing procedures using the computer as an audit tool refer to
questions.explanation: CAATs = using computer tools for audit procedures.

questions.questionText: Consists of generalized computer programs designed to perform common audit tasks or standardized data processing functions.
options: A. Package or generalized audit software
questions.correctAnswer: A. Package or generalized audit software
questions.explanation: GAS (e.g., ACL, IDEA) are generalized audit software.

exams.examName: Public Sector & Civic Societies Model Exam @2016

questions.questionText: Which of the following would not be considered a government or nonprofit organization?
options: A software company that sells software exclusively to state and local governments.
A private trust organized for charitable purposes
questions.correctAnswer: A software company that sells software exclusively to state and local governments.
questions.explanation: A for-profit business entity (even if selling only to governments) is not classified as a government or nonprofit organization.

questions.questionText: Which of the following characteristics best distinguishes a government entity from a business entity?
options: Governments operate in a very small section of the economy while businesses operate globally.
Cost analysis and other control and evaluation techniques are essential to ensure that resources are used economically and efficiently.
Those contributing resources to the entity do not necessarily receive a direct or proportionate share the services.
Businesses must acquire and convert scarce resources while governments can demand whatever they need.
questions.correctAnswer: Those contributing resources to the entity do not necessarily receive a direct or proportionate share the services.
questions.explanation: The defining feature of governments is non-exchange transactions: taxpayers do not receive direct or proportional benefits in return for contributions.

questions.questionText: Which source of financial resources is unique to governments?
questions.explanation: Compulsory taxation (non-exchange revenue) is a sovereign power unique to governments.

questions.questionText: The primary purpose of a fund is
options: To provide expenditure authority for a government or not-for-profit organization.
To segregate an organization's resources according to the purpose(s) for which they are to be used.
To keep an organization's constituency from demanding that the organization utilize resources that it wants to save for a specific future objective.
To confuse and confound the legislative body as to the use and purpose of government resources.
questions.correctAnswer: To segregate an organization's resources according to the purpose(s) for which they are to be used.
questions.explanation: Funds exist to segregate and restrict resources for specific purposes (GASB Concept Statement No. 1).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a fund?
questions.explanation: Funds are accounting and fiscal entities with self-balancing accounts, but they are not separate legal entities (the government itself is the legal entity).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a fund category used by state and local governments?
questions.explanation: GASB recognizes three fund categories: governmental, proprietary, and fiduciary. No 'Plant and Equipment' category exists.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an official fund category used by state and local governments?
questions.explanation: Governmental funds is one of the three main categories defined by GASB.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered a proprietary fund?
questions.explanation: Proprietary funds consist of Enterprise Funds and Internal Service Funds.

questions.questionText: The operations of a city bus line receiving all its funding from user charges would be accounted for in
questions.explanation: Activities financed primarily by user charges and serving the public are reported in Enterprise Funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not considered a fiduciary fund?
questions.explanation: Permanent Funds are governmental funds, not fiduciary funds.

questions.questionText: Activities of a central motor pool that provides and services vehicles for the use of municipal employees on official business should be accounted for in
questions.explanation: Internal Service Funds account for goods/services provided primarily to other government departments on a cost-reimbursement basis.

questions.questionText: A government can only have one
questions.explanation: GASB requires exactly one General Fund per government; other fund types may have multiple or none.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not considered a governmental fund?
questions.explanation: Internal Service Funds are proprietary funds, not governmental funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following uses the flow of economic resources measurement focus?
questions.explanation: Proprietary funds (including Internal Service Funds) use the economic resources measurement focus and full accrual basis.

questions.questionText: Proprietary funds recognize
options: Expenditures when the fund incurs a liability for goods or services.
Expenditures when the fund uses goods or services.
Expenses when the fund incurs a liability for goods or services.
Expenses when the fund uses goods or services.
questions.correctAnswer: Expenses when the fund incurs a liability for goods or services.
questions.explanation: Proprietary funds use full accrual accounting and recognize expenses when liabilities are incurred (matching principle).

questions.questionText: Which of the following uses the flow of current financial resources measurement focus?
questions.explanation: Governmental funds (including Special Revenue Funds) use the current financial resources measurement focus and modified accrual basis.

questions.questionText: The availability criterion for recognizing revenues applies to all of the following funds except
questions.explanation: The 'available' criterion is part of modified accrual (used in governmental funds); Enterprise Funds use full accrual.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a characteristic of the General Fund?
options: Is used to account for all financial resources that are not restricted, committed, or assigned to a specific purpose and consequently accounted for in another fund.
Is used by all governments that report governmental fund activities.
Requires a combining statement at year end for governments that have more than one General Fund.
Is established at inception of a government and exists throughout its life.
questions.correctAnswer: Requires a combining statement at year end for governments that have more than one General Fund.
questions.explanation: A government is permitted only one General Fund; combining statements are not required for multiple General Funds because they do not exist.

questions.questionText: A Special Revenue Fund
options: Is used to account for resources restricted or committed to expenditures for capital outlay or debt service purposes.
Must be used to account for all expendable restricted or committed resources.
Must include resources from a revenue source that is restricted or committed to expenditures for specific purposes other than debt service or capital outlay.
Must be used to account for all nonexpendable, restricted or committed resources
questions.correctAnswer: Must include resources from a revenue source that is restricted or committed to expenditures for specific purposes other than debt service or capital outlay.
questions.explanation: Special Revenue Funds are used for specific restricted/committed revenue sources (excluding major capital projects and debt service).

questions.questionText: A school district receives a federal grant of $200,000 that is restricted to support a program... Which of the following funds could be used for this activity?
questions.explanation: Restricted grants for specific programs are typically accounted for in Special Revenue Funds.

questions.questionText: A new computer, which had been estimated to cost $28,000, was received for an activity of a special revenue fund. The actual cost of the computer was $29,400. To record this in the special revenue fund,
options: Capital assets should be debited for $29,400.
There is no entry in the special revenue fund. The General Capital Assets account should be debited for $28,000.
questions.explanation: Governmental funds use modified accrual and record expenditures at the actual amount incurred (purchase price).

questions.questionText: Taxes receivable of $80,000, which have a related allowance for uncollectible taxes of $8,000, become delinquent. The entry to record this includes a debit to
questions.explanation: When taxes become delinquent, the allowance is reclassified from current to delinquent.

questions.questionText: Accounts receivables are determined to be uncollectible and are written off. The following account should be debited:
questions.explanation: Write-offs debit the allowance account (contra-asset), not expense (already recognized when allowance was established).

questions.questionText: A government levies property taxes of $2,500,000, 1% of which are expected to prove uncollectible. The property taxes should be reported in the General Fund statement of revenues, expenditures, and changes in fund balances as
options: Revenues of $2,500,000 and other financing uses of $25,000.
Revenues of $2,475,000 and no expenditures or other financing uses.
Other financing sources of $2,500,000 and expenditures of $25,000
questions.correctAnswer: Revenues of $2,475,000 and no expenditures or other financing uses.
questions.explanation: Under modified accrual, property taxes are recorded net of estimated uncollectibles as revenue when measurable and available.

questions.questionText: Under the modified accrual basis, revenues are considered available to finance current period expenditures if they are legally usable to finance expenditures of the period and
options: Collected in the current period or soon enough thereafter to be used to pay liabilities of the current period.
questions.correctAnswer: Collected in the current period or soon enough thereafter to be used to pay liabilities of the current period.
questions.explanation: The 'available' criterion (usually within 60 days after year-end) is the key for revenue recognition in governmental funds.

questions.questionText: Expenditures are defined as
options: Uses of current financial resources other than for capital asset purchases and transfers.
Decreases in net current financial resources other than from specified transactions.
Changes in liabilities and deferred inflows.
questions.correctAnswer: Uses of current financial resources other than for capital asset purchases and transfers.
questions.explanation: GASB defines expenditures in governmental funds as decreases in current financial resources (except capital outlays and transfers).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a typical governmental fund liability, and thus not an expenditure that is recognized when the liability is incurred?
questions.explanation: Governmental funds recognize expenditures for long-term liabilities only when due (current portion); long-term portions are not recorded in fund statements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following capital asset-related transactions would most likely be accounted for through a Capital Projects Fund?
options: A major general government capital lease transaction.
Purchase of multiple computers for general government departments.
Construction of a general government office building.
Maintenance of general government fixed assets.
questions.correctAnswer: Construction of a general government office building.
questions.explanation: Capital Projects Funds are used for acquisition or construction of major capital facilities.

questions.questionText: If a governmental entity issued a six-month, $400,000 note payable at 6% interest three months prior to the fiscal year end... Capital Projects Fund interest payable should be accrued as of the end of the fiscal year in the amount of
questions.explanation: Three months interest = $400,000 × 6% × 3/12 = $6,000. Governmental funds accrue interest only when due, but if the note is short-term and due within the year, accrual may be required.

questions.questionText: Revenues in a Debt Service Fund are recognized when
questions.explanation: Debt Service Funds (governmental funds) use modified accrual → revenues recognized when measurable and available.

questions.questionText: Equity in a Debt Service Fund is known as
questions.explanation: Governmental funds report equity as fund balance (not net position).

questions.questionText: What measurement focus does a Debt Service Fund use?
questions.explanation: All governmental funds use current financial resources measurement focus.

questions.questionText: A government is required to use a Debt Service Fund in which of the following cases?
options: When financial resources are being accumulated for long-term general government principal and interest maturing in future years.
questions.correctAnswer: When financial resources are being accumulated for long-term general government principal and interest maturing in future years.
questions.explanation: Debt Service Funds are required when resources are accumulated in advance for future debt service.

questions.questionText: Principal and interest expenditures on general long-term debt should be recognized in the period
options: Prior to the year in which they are due, i.e., when they become short-term debt.
That they are legally due and payable.
questions.correctAnswer: That they are legally due and payable.
questions.explanation: Governmental funds recognize debt service expenditures when legally due (modified accrual).

questions.questionText: Internal Service Fund is considered to be
options: Either a governmental fund or a proprietary fund, depending on the nature of the activity accounted for within the fund.
questions.explanation: Internal Service Funds are classified as proprietary funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following methods of capital asset valuation is consistent with generally accepted accounting principles for a donated capital asset?
questions.explanation: GASB requires donated capital assets to be recorded at acquisition value (estimated fair value at date of donation).

questions.questionText: Which of the following capital assets would not be considered a general capital asset?
options: Land at the local municipal park
A highway bridge maintained by a city government
Infrastructure associated with the local water system
questions.correctAnswer: Infrastructure associated with the local water system
questions.explanation: Water system infrastructure is reported in the Enterprise Fund (proprietary), not as general capital assets.

questions.questionText: The parks and recreation department... purchased a new athletic field mower... The General Fund would report depreciation expense at the end of Year 2 in the amount of
questions.explanation: Governmental funds (including General Fund) do not record depreciation expense; depreciation is reported only in government-wide statements.

questions.questionText: When charges to external users are a principal revenue source... the use of an Enterprise Fund is required... except
options: When user fees are charged for the majority of the activity’s operations.
When an activity is financed with debt that is secured solely by the pledge of revenues.
When laws and regulations require that the activity's costs be recovered with fees and charges.
When pricing policies of the activity establish fees and charges are designed for cost recovery.
questions.correctAnswer: When pricing policies of the activity establish fees and charges are designed for cost recovery.
questions.explanation: Cost recovery pricing alone does not require Enterprise Fund classification; other criteria (debt pledge, legal requirement, majority user fees) do.

questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions does not require that an activity... be reported in an Enterprise Fund?
options: Net revenues are pledged as the sole security for debt issued to finance the activity.
Laws or regulations require the activity to recover its costs, including capital costs.
Pricing policies require the activity to recover its costs, including capital costs.
The primary source of revenue for the activity is charges to external users
questions.correctAnswer: Pricing policies require the activity to recover its costs, including capital costs.
questions.explanation: Pricing policy alone is not sufficient to mandate Enterprise Fund use; legal requirement or debt pledge is stronger.

questions.questionText: A city Enterprise Fund was awarded an operating grant... The Enterprise Fund will report this grant... as
questions.explanation: Operating grants in Enterprise Funds are typically reported as nonoperating revenues (unless directly related to core operations).

questions.questionText: The Central Warehouse Internal Service Fund purchased $15,000 of inventory on account... Which of the following statements regarding the accounting for the transaction is false?
options: Expenses in the Internal Service Fund will increase.
Capital assets recorded in the Internal Service Fund remain unchanged.
The transaction will increase total assets.
The transaction will increase total liabilities.
questions.correctAnswer: Expenses in the Internal Service Fund will increase.
questions.explanation: Purchase of inventory increases inventory (asset) and accounts payable (liability) — no immediate expense until consumed.

questions.questionText: The General Fund paid $4,000 to the Internal Service Fund for services rendered. Which of the following statements accurately reflects the reporting effects of the transaction?
options: The Internal Service Fund will report revenues of $4,000.
The Internal Service Fund will report capital contributions of $4,000.
The Internal Service will report a transfer in of $4,000.
The Internal Service Fund will record a direct adjustment to unrestricted net position.
questions.correctAnswer: The Internal Service Fund will report revenues of $4,000.
questions.explanation: Billings to other funds for services are operating revenues in the Internal Service Fund.

questions.questionText: The General Fund contributes $40,000 to an Internal Service Fund to subsidize its operations... The Internal Service Fund will report this contribution as a
options: Direct equity adjustment to restricted net position.
questions.explanation: Non-capital contributions/subsidies between funds are reported as transfers.

questions.questionText: An other postemployment benefit plan where assets have been placed in trust would be reported as
options: As a Pension and Other Employee Benefit Trust Fund.
questions.correctAnswer: As a Pension and Other Employee Benefit Trust Fund.
questions.explanation: OPEB plans with trust assets are reported in Pension (and Other Employee Benefit) Trust Funds (fiduciary).

questions.questionText: Which types of funds are classified as fiduciary funds?
options: Pension trust, permanent trust, private-purpose trust, and investment trust funds.
Pension trust, permanent trust, and agency funds.
Pension trust, private-purpose trust, investment trust, and agency funds.
Expendable trust, nonexpendable trust, pension trust, and investment trust funds.
questions.correctAnswer: Pension trust, private-purpose trust, investment trust, and agency funds.
questions.explanation: GASB classifies fiduciary funds as pension trust, investment trust, private-purpose trust, and custodial (formerly agency) funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following activities would most likely be accounted for in an Agency Fund...
options: Tax collections by a county on behalf of local municipalities.
A Federal pass-through grant where the primary government has administrative involvement in the grant program.
Special assessments for debt on which the government is not obligated in any manner
questions.correctAnswer: Tax collections by a county on behalf of local municipalities.
questions.explanation: Agency (custodial) funds account for resources held purely in a custodial capacity for others.

questions.questionText: A government receives a donation of $300,000 to establish an endowment... The government should report this activity in which type of fund?
questions.explanation: Endowment benefiting non-government parties (high school students outside the government) is a private-purpose trust fund.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accounts would typically be reported in an agency fund?
questions.explanation: Agency/custodial funds report liabilities to the parties for whom resources are held (e.g., Due to Other Governments).

questions.questionText: A government establishes an Investment Trust Fund... The Investment Trust Fund should report this activity in the statement of changes in net position as
questions.explanation: Fiduciary funds use 'additions' and 'deductions' instead of revenues and expenses.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true concerning accounting and financial reporting practices related to capital asset acquisitions?
options: Routine capital purchases such as vehicles and equipment often may be financed and accounted for in a General Fund.
Most capital lease transactions related to governmental funds are accounted for initially in either the General Fund or a Debt Service Fund.
Capital Project Funds may be used only for acquisition or construction of major capital facilities.
Most capital projects last only for on fiscal year.
questions.correctAnswer: Routine capital purchases such as vehicles and equipment often may be financed and accounted for in a General Fund.
questions.explanation: Small/routine capital acquisitions are often recorded directly in the General Fund or other governmental funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true?
options: A government is required to record each major general government capital p...(truncated)
questions.correctAnswer: A government is required to record each major general government capital purchase in the General Capital Assets account.
questions.explanation: In fund statements, capital assets are not recorded in governmental funds; they are reported only in government-wide statements.

questions.questionText: Salaries and wages of $550,000 were paid during the year. At the end of the fiscal year, salaries and wages payable was $12,000. The General Fund would report salaries and wages expenditures for the year of
questions.explanation: Modified accrual: expenditures = cash paid + ending payable – beginning payable = $550,000 + $12,000 = $562,000 (assuming beginning payable was $0).

questions.questionText: Which of the following governmental fund expenditures would not be considered a current operating expenditure?
questions.explanation: Capital outlay is a capital expenditure, not a current operating expenditure.

questions.questionText: Expenditures in a governmental fund are recognized when due for
questions.explanation: Debt service expenditures (principal and interest) are recognized when legally due.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a managerial problem associated with expenditures?
options: Misallocation or poor allotments of appropriations.
questions.explanation: The availability criterion is an accounting concept, not a typical managerial expenditure problem.

questions.questionText: Assume that the Village of Hannah uses the purchases method of inventory accounting... What entry would be made to reflect the inventory increase?
options: Debit Expenditures, Credit Inventory of Supplies.
Debit Inventory of Supplies, Credit Other Financing Sources.
Debit Expenditures, Credit Other Financing Sources.
Debit Inventory of Supplies, Credit Expenditures.
questions.correctAnswer: Debit Inventory of Supplies, Credit Other Financing Sources.
questions.explanation: Under purchases method, year-end inventory increase is credited to Other Financing Sources (not reducing expenditures).

questions.questionText: Assume that a government purchases $85,000 of inventory... The General Fund should report
options: Other financing source of $20,000 for the year.
Other financing use of $20,000 for the year
questions.explanation: Consumption method: expenditures = purchases – increase in inventory = $85,000 – ($35,000 – $15,000) = $65,000.

questions.questionText: If a government uses a perpetual inventory system... and there is an inventory overage... the inventory asset account should
options: Be increased and the expenditure account decreased.
Be decreased and the expenditure account increased.
Remain the same. The expenditure account will be decreased, offset by an allowance for inventory overage account.
Remain the same. The expenditure account will be increased, offset by an allowance for inventory overage account.
questions.correctAnswer: Be increased and the expenditure account decreased.
questions.explanation: Inventory overage increases the asset and reduces expenditures (consumption method).

questions.questionText: A government has $3,000,000 of 6%, 10-year general obligation bonds... What is the minimum amount of interest expenditures... for the year ended December 31, 20X7?
questions.explanation: Interest expenditures are recognized when legally due. If no interest payment is due by year-end, no expenditure is recognized.

questions.questionText: A government has $3,000,000 of 6%, 10-year general obligation bonds... What is the maximum amount of interest expenditures... for the year ended December 31, 20X7?
questions.explanation: Maximum = full year interest = $3,000,000 × 6% = $180,000, but since issued July 2, only half-year interest is accrued if due.

questions.questionText: A government retired $5,000,000 of outstanding general obligation bonds when due... The government should report this transaction in its Debt Service Fund as
options: Other financing uses of $3,000,000 and expenditures of $2,000,000.
Other financing uses of $2,000,000 and expenditures of $3,000,000
questions.correctAnswer: Other financing uses of $3,000,000 and expenditures of $2,000,000.
questions.explanation: Refunding portion ($3M new bonds) = other financing use; accumulated resources ($2M) = expenditure.

questions.questionText: A Debt Service Fund received an annual payment from the General Fund to finance upcoming debt service payments. The amount received... should be reported... as
questions.explanation: Interfund transfers to Debt Service Funds are reported as other financing sources.

questions.questionText: A Debt Service Fund received a $100,000 payment from the General Fund... payments of $50,000 interest and $60,000 principal... The Debt Service Fund statement... should report
options: An excess of revenues over expenditures of $50,000.
An excess of expenditures over revenues of $10,000.
An excess of expenditures over revenues of $50,000.
An excess of expenditures over revenues of $110,000.
questions.correctAnswer: An excess of expenditures over revenues of $10,000.
questions.explanation: Revenues = $0; Other financing sources = $100,000; Expenditures = $110,000 → excess expenditures $10,000.

questions.questionText: Debt Service Fund expenditures would include all of the following except
options: Repayment of refunded bonds using resources transferred from the General Fund.
questions.explanation: Discounts/premiums on refunding are part of other financing sources/uses, not expenditures.

questions.questionText: A Debt Service Fund should be used to account for debt service on special assessment indebtedness
options: Unless the government is not legally obligated for the debt.
If the government is obligated in some manner for the debt.
Never. A Special Assessment Fund should be used.
questions.correctAnswer: If the government is obligated in some manner for the debt.
questions.explanation: If the government is obligated in any way for special assessment debt, it is accounted for in Debt Service Fund.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not usually a requirement of a Debt Service Fund (DSF) for a term bond issue?
options: The DSF should be used to accumulate the necessary funds to pay the term bonds when they come due.
The DSF makes periodic interest payment on the debt during its life.
The DSF will have funded reserves as required by the debt covenant.
A DSF that services a term bond issue is used to account for principal retirement only, with interest expenditures made directly from the General Fund.
questions.correctAnswer: A DSF that services a term bond issue is used to account for principal retirement only, with interest expenditures made directly from the General Fund.
questions.explanation: Term bonds require accumulation for principal; interest is typically paid from DSF as well.

questions.questionText: The City of Newport issued $1,500,000 of general obligation refunding bonds at a 2% premium... Debt Service Fund Expenditures will be debited for
questions.explanation: Payment to defease old debt = face + premium – issuance costs = expenditures.

questions.questionText: Apex County advance refunded $3,000,000 of outstanding bonds... Which of the following statements about the reporting... is not true?
options: Net other financing sources and uses of $500,000.
questions.correctAnswer: Net other financing sources and uses of $500,000.
questions.explanation: Refunding proceeds = other financing source; payment to escrow = other financing use; net is zero for refunding portion.

questions.questionText: Monica City paid $6,000,000 to its fiscal agent... deemed defeased in-substance. The city should report... in its Debt Service Fund as
options: Other financing uses of $3,000,000 and expenditures of $3,000,000.
Other financing uses of $5,000,000 and expenditures of $1,000,000.
questions.correctAnswer: Other financing uses of $3,000,000 and expenditures of $3,000,000.
questions.explanation: Refunding portion = other financing use; accumulated resources = expenditure.

questions.questionText: A government paid $6,000,000 into an irrevocable trust... but the transaction does not meet the defeasance in-substance criteria...
options: Other financing uses of $3,000,000 and expenditures of $3,000,000.
No expenditures or other financing uses should be reported
questions.explanation: If not in-substance defeasance, the entire payment is treated as debt retirement expenditure.

questions.questionText: Wartrace City’s Communications Enterprise Fund... was awarded a $400,000 federal grant... As of December 31, 20X7, the Communications Enterprise Fund should
questions.explanation: Operating grants are recognized as revenue when qualifying expenditures are incurred (eligibility met).

questions.questionText: A city's Enterprise Fund issued revenue bonds with a face value of $10,000,000... total other financing sources in the amount of
questions.explanation: Enterprise Funds report bond proceeds as liabilities (not other financing sources).

questions.questionText: An Enterprise Fund is donating equipment to a general government department... The entry... would include
options: A debit to nonoperating expense of $25,000.
A debit to transfer out of $28,000.
A debit to capital contribution of $25,000.
A debit to nonoperating expense of $28,000
questions.correctAnswer: A debit to nonoperating expense of $25,000.
questions.explanation: Donations of assets are recorded at book value as nonoperating expense (loss).

questions.questionText: A developer agreed to pay for water and wastewater infrastructure... The entry... when the project is complete would be
options: A debit to capital assets and a credit to net investment in capital assets.
A debit to capital assets and a credit to capital contribution.
A debit to capital assets and a credit to transfer in.
A debit to capital assets and a credit to nonoperating revenues
questions.correctAnswer: A debit to capital assets and a credit to capital contribution.
questions.explanation: Developer-contributed assets are recorded as capital contributions in proprietary funds.

questions.questionText: An Enterprise Fund contributed $85,000 to the General Fund for operations... Which of the following statements is true?
options: The Enterprise Fund will report capital contributions of $85,000.
The Enterprise Fund will report other financing uses of $85,000.
The Enterprise Fund will report advances of $85,000.
The Enterprise Fund will report transfers out of $85,000.
questions.correctAnswer: The Enterprise Fund will report transfers out of $85,000.
questions.explanation: Non-repayable contributions to other funds are reported as transfers out.

questions.questionText: An Enterprise Fund entered into a capital lease... In the year of inception the Enterprise Fund would report
options: An other financing use of $270,000 and expenses of $30,000.
questions.explanation: Proprietary funds record capital leases as assets and liabilities at present value.

questions.questionText: The Public Utilities Enterprise Fund was ordered by the court to pay environmental damages of $500,000... In the year of the judgment, the Enterprise Fund would report
options: Nothing. All amounts would be recorded in General Long-term Liabilities accounts.
questions.explanation: Enterprise Funds use full accrual → recognize full liability and expense when probable and estimable.

questions.questionText: The Central Warehouse Internal Service Fund purchased $15,000 of inventory on account... Which of the following statements... is false?
options: Expenses in the Internal Service Fund will increase.
Capital assets recorded in the Internal Service Fund remain unchanged.
The transaction will increase total assets.
The transaction will increase total liabilities.
questions.correctAnswer: Expenses in the Internal Service Fund will increase.
questions.explanation: Inventory purchase increases assets and liabilities — expense occurs when inventory is used.

questions.questionText: An Internal Service Fund had investments... fair market value... $85,000. The Internal Service Fund would
options: Report a reduction of revenue of $15,000.
Not adjust the value of the investments reported on the balance sheet.
Report a loss on investments of $15,000.
questions.correctAnswer: Report a loss on investments of $15,000.
questions.explanation: Proprietary funds adjust investments to fair value with unrealized gains/losses recognized in income.

questions.questionText: The General Fund paid $4,000 to the Internal Service Fund for services rendered...
options: The Internal Service Fund will report revenues of $4,000.
The Internal Service Fund will report capital contributions of $4,000.
The Internal Service will report a transfer in of $4,000.
The Internal Service Fund will record a direct adjustment to unrestricted net position.
questions.correctAnswer: The Internal Service Fund will report revenues of $4,000.
questions.explanation: Charges for services to other funds are operating revenues in Internal Service Funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would most likely be accounted for in an Internal Service Fund?
options: A government's water and sewer department if it provides water and sewer services to government departments as well as to residents and businesses in the community.
A government's central printing shop that provides a very minimal amount of services to a few outside customers.
The Payroll and Benefits Department of the government.
A consolidated supplies facility where most of the customers are other governments.
questions.correctAnswer: The Payroll and Benefits Department of the government.
questions.explanation: Centralized support services provided primarily to other departments are typical Internal Service Fund activities.

questions.questionText: The Tullahoma School District’s Print Shop Internal Service Fund received $25,000 from a state grant... will report this contribution as a
options: Direct equity adjustment to restricted net position.
questions.explanation: Grants restricted for capital purposes in proprietary funds are reported as capital contributions.

questions.questionText: Transfers from an Internal Service fund to another fund are reported in the Internal Service Fund’s Statement of Cash Flows as
options: Cash flows from noncapital financing activities.
Cash flows from capital and related financing activities.
questions.correctAnswer: Cash flows from noncapital financing activities.
questions.explanation: Interfund transfers are classified as noncapital financing activities in proprietary fund cash flow statements.

questions.questionText: In an Internal Service Fund, the expectation is that
options: Each year's revenues should equal each year's expenses because the revenues are simply an allocation of that year's expenses.
Each year's revenues should equal each year's expenditures because the revenues are simply an allocation of that year's expenditures.
Accumulated revenues over time should approximately equal the accumulated expenses over time.
Expenses will exceed revenues because depreciation expense is reported in an Internal Service Fund.
questions.correctAnswer: Accumulated revenues over time should approximately equal the accumulated expenses over time.
questions.explanation: Internal Service Funds are intended to break even over the long term (cost recovery).

questions.questionText: All of the following transactions could potentially be reconciling items between the governmental fund financial statements and government-wide governmental activities column except
options: Borrowing from a local bank with a short-term loan
questions.correctAnswer: Borrowing from a local bank with a short-term loan
questions.explanation: Short-term borrowing is recorded similarly in fund and government-wide statements (no reconciliation needed).

questions.questionText: Which of the following adjustments will not be necessary to convert the measurement focus and basis of accounting found in the governmental funds to the governmental activities reported in the government-wide financial statements?
options: Recording expenses with no corresponding expenditures.
Converting “when due” payables to accrual based payables.
Eliminating expenditures with no expense counterparts.
Adjusting the fair value of investments.
questions.correctAnswer: Adjusting the fair value of investments.
questions.explanation: Governmental funds already report investments at fair value; no adjustment needed for government-wide.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would be reported as a capital asset in the government-wide financial statements?
options: Infrastructure assets of an Enterprise Fund.
Land held for resale by a Capital Projects Fund.
Buildings used in general government operations.
Equipment used in an Internal Service Fund.
questions.correctAnswer: Buildings used in general government operations.
questions.explanation: General government buildings are general capital assets in governmental activities.

questions.questionText: In government-wide financial statements, long-term liabilities are reported
options: In both governmental and business-type activities.
Only if they are due within one year.
questions.correctAnswer: In both governmental and business-type activities.
questions.explanation: Government-wide statements report all long-term liabilities using full accrual.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding the reconciliation between fund balances and net position?
options: Capital assets are added to fund balances.
Long-term liabilities are subtracted from fund balances.
questions.explanation: Reconciliation includes adding capital assets, subtracting long-term liabilities, adjusting deferred inflows/outflows, etc.

questions.questionText: The government-wide statement of activities reports program revenues from
options: Charges for services and operating grants.
questions.correctAnswer: Charges for services and operating grants.
questions.explanation: Program revenues include charges for services, operating grants, and capital grants.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not reported as a separate column in the government-wide statement of net position?
questions.explanation: Fiduciary funds are reported separately, not in the government-wide statements.

questions.questionText: In the government-wide financial statements, depreciation expense is allocated to
questions.explanation: Government-wide statements allocate depreciation to functional/program categories.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding infrastructure assets in government-wide statements?
options: They must be depreciated using the straight-line method.
Governments may use the modified approach instead of depreciation.
They are reported only in business-type activities.
They are not reported in government-wide statements.
questions.correctAnswer: Governments may use the modified approach instead of depreciation.
questions.explanation: GASB allows the modified approach (asset management system + condition preservation) for infrastructure.

questions.questionText: The reconciliation of the change in fund balances to change in net position includes adding back
questions.explanation: Capital outlays and debt principal are expenditures in funds but not expenses in government-wide.

questions.questionText: Which statement is required for fiduciary funds?
options: Statement of revenues, expenditures, and changes in fund balances.
Statement of fiduciary net position and statement of changes in fiduciary net position.
questions.correctAnswer: Statement of fiduciary net position and statement of changes in fiduciary net position.
questions.explanation: Fiduciary funds use economic resources focus and report net position and changes therein.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a required basic financial statement for state and local governments?
options: Fund financial statements for governmental funds.
Budgetary comparison statement for the General Fund and major special revenue funds.
questions.correctAnswer: Budgetary comparison statement for the General Fund and major special revenue funds.
questions.explanation: Budgetary comparisons are RSI (Required Supplementary Information), not basic financial statements.

questions.questionText: Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) is presented
options: As part of the basic financial statements.
Immediately before the basic financial statements.
As part of the notes to the financial statements.
questions.correctAnswer: Immediately before the basic financial statements.
questions.explanation: MD&A is introductory information presented before the basic financial statements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding component units?
options: They are always blended into the primary government.
They may be blended or discretely presented.
They are reported only in fiduciary funds.
They are never included in government-wide statements.
questions.correctAnswer: They may be blended or discretely presented.
questions.explanation: GASB requires component units to be either blended (integral part) or discretely presented (separate column).

questions.questionText: The focus of government-wide financial statements is on
questions.explanation: Government-wide statements focus on operational accountability (full accrual, long-term view), while fund statements focus on fiscal accountability.

exams.examName: Advanced Financial Accounting 2 Model Exit Exam @2016

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a reason for a company to expand through a combination, rather than by building new facilities?
options: A combination might provide cost advantages.
A combination might provide fewer operating delays.
A combination might provide easier access to intangible assets.
A combination might provide an opportunity to invest in a company without having to take responsibility for its financial results.
questions.correctAnswer: D. A combination might provide an opportunity to invest in a company without having to take responsibility for its financial results.
questions.explanation: Business combinations involve obtaining control and responsibility for the acquiree's operations and results. Passive investment without control is not the purpose of a combination.

questions.questionText: A business merger differs from a business consolidation because
options: A merger dissolves all but one of the prior entities, but a consolidation dissolves all of the prior entities and forms a new corporation.
A consolidation dissolves all but one of the prior entities, but a merger dissolves all of the prior entities.
A merger is created when two entities join, but a consolidation is created when more than two entities join.
A consolidation is created when two entities join, but a merger is created when more than two entities join.
questions.correctAnswer: A. A merger dissolves all but one of the prior entities, but a consolidation dissolves all of the prior entities and forms a new corporation.
questions.explanation: Merger: one entity survives. Consolidation: all entities dissolve and a new one is formed.

questions.questionText: The cost of an acquiree in a business combination includes all the following except:
questions.correctAnswer: C. Current fair value of PPE.
questions.explanation: Consideration transferred (cost) includes direct costs, debt at FV, contingent consideration. Fair value of acquiree's PPE is used in allocation, not in measuring cost.

questions.questionText: A target company’s defense against an unfriendly takeover that involves the disposal of one or more profitable business segments of the target is termed:
questions.explanation: Scorched earth defense: selling valuable assets to reduce attractiveness to acquirer.

questions.questionText: Following the IFRS 3 definition of a business combination, a business combination occurs when a company acquires an equity interest in another entity and has
options: At least 20% ownership in the entity.
More than 50% ownership in the entity.
control over the entity, irrespective of the percentage owned
questions.correctAnswer: D. control over the entity, irrespective of the percentage owned
questions.explanation: IFRS 3 defines business combination as obtaining **control** (per IFRS 10), not tied to a specific % ownership.

questions.questionText: In a completed working paper elimination... on the date of the business combination, the total of the debits generally equals the:
options: Parent company’s total cost of its investment in the subsidiary.
Carrying amount of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Total paid-in capital of the subsidiary.
questions.correctAnswer: A. Parent company’s total cost of its investment in the subsidiary.
questions.explanation: Elimination debits subsidiary equity + fair value adjustments + goodwill = parent's investment cost.

questions.questionText: The traditional definition of control for a parent company–subsidiary relationship... emphasizes:
options: Both legal form and economic substance.
Neither legal form nor economic substance.
questions.explanation: Traditional >50% voting interest rule is legal/form-based (pre-IFRS 10).

questions.questionText: A parent need not present consolidated financial statements if it meets all the following conditions:
options: It is a wholly-owned subsidiary or is a partially-owned subsidiary of another entity and all its other owners.
Its debt or equity instruments are not traded in a public market
It did not file, nor is it in the process of filing, its financial statements with a securities commission...
An investor controls an investee when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns...
questions.explanation: IFRS 10 provides this exact exemption from consolidation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true according to IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements issued by IASB?
options: An investor controls an investee when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns... through its power over the investee
An investor has power over an investee when the investor has existing rights that give it the current ability to direct the relevant activities...
An investor is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns... as a result of the investee’s performance.
A parent shall prepare consolidated financial statements using different accounting policies...
questions.correctAnswer: A. An investor controls an investee when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns... through its power over the investee
questions.explanation: This is the core definition of control in IFRS 10.

questions.questionText: In a working paper elimination... the subtotal of the debits to the subsidiary’s stockholders’ equity accounts equals the:
options: Current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Current fair value of the subsidiary’s total net assets, including goodwill.
Balance of the parent company’s investment ledger account.
Carrying amount of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets
questions.correctAnswer: D. Carrying amount of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets
questions.explanation: Equity elimination uses subsidiary's book value (carrying amount); fair value adjustments are separate.

questions.questionText: In the working paper for consolidated balance sheet... the total of the Eliminations column is equal to:
options: The current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
The total stockholder’s equity of the subsidiary.
The current fair value of the subsidiary’s total net assets, including goodwill.
An amount that is not determinable
questions.correctAnswer: C. The current fair value of the subsidiary’s total net assets, including goodwill.
questions.explanation: Total elimination balances to investment cost = subsidiary equity (book) + FV adjustments + goodwill.

questions.questionText: In a business combination... goodwill developed in the working paper elimination is attributed:
options: In its entirety to the subsidiary.
In its entirety to the parent company.
To both the parent company and the subsidiary, in the ratio of current fair values of identifiable net assets.
In its entirety to the consolidated entity.
questions.correctAnswer: D. In its entirety to the consolidated entity.
questions.explanation: Goodwill is a consolidated group asset, not attributed to parent or subsidiary individually.

questions.questionText: On the date of the business combination of a parent company and its partially owned subsidiary... the amount assigned to minority interest in net assets of subsidiary is based on the:
options: Cost of the parent company’s investment in the subsidiary’s common stock.
Carrying amount of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Current fair value of the subsidiary’s total net assets, including goodwill
questions.correctAnswer: C. Current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
questions.explanation: Under IFRS 3 (full goodwill option), NCI can be measured at proportionate share of identifiable net assets at fair value.

questions.questionText: Under the equity method... dividends declared by the subsidiary to the parent company are accounted for by the parent company as:
options: Dividend revenue on the declaration date.
A reduction of the investment in subsidiary on the payment date.
Dividend revenue on the payment date.
A reduction of the investment in subsidiary on the declaration date
questions.correctAnswer: D. A reduction of the investment in subsidiary on the declaration date
questions.explanation: Equity method treats dividends as return of investment (reduce carrying amount) when declared.

questions.questionText: Under the equity method of accounting, dividends declared by the subsidiary to the parent company are credited to the parent’s:
options: Investment in Subsidiary Common Stock account.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Investment in Subsidiary Common Stock account.
questions.explanation: Dividends reduce the investment account under equity method.

questions.questionText: After completion of the parent company’s equity-method journal entries... the balance of the parent’s Intercompany Investment Income ledger is equal to the:
options: Subsidiary’s net Income, less amortization of current fair value differences of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Subsidiary’s net income, less amortization of current fair value differences of the subsidiary’s net assets, including goodwill.
Increase in the after-closing balance of the subsidiary’s Retained Earnings ledger account
questions.correctAnswer: B. Subsidiary’s net Income, less amortization of current fair value differences of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
questions.explanation: Equity method income = subsidiary NI adjusted for amortization of FV differentials (goodwill not amortized under IFRS).

questions.questionText: If a parent company uses the equity method... the amount eliminated for the subsidiary’s retained earnings is the balance of the subsidiary’s Retained Earnings Ledger account:
options: At the beginning of the year.
On the date of the business combination.
At the end of the year.
At the beginning of the year, less the balance of the parent’s Retained Earnings of Subsidiary account.
questions.correctAnswer: A. At the beginning of the year.
questions.explanation: Beginning RE is eliminated; post-acquisition change is already reflected in parent's equity-method entries.

questions.questionText: If $1.9672 is required to acquire one British pound, the amount of pound(s) required to acquire $1 is:
questions.explanation: Reciprocal rate = 1 ÷ 1.9672 ≈ £0.5083 per $1.

questions.questionText: On April 30, 2005... the U.S. enterprise may convert the LCU100,000 draft to:
questions.explanation: Settlement uses the buying rate (bank pays) = LCU 100,000 × $0.15 = $15,000.

questions.questionText: In a completed working paper elimination... the total of the debits generally equals the:
options: Parent company’s total cost of its investment in the subsidiary.
Carrying amount of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Total paid-in capital of the subsidiary.
questions.correctAnswer: A. Parent company’s total cost of its investment in the subsidiary.
questions.explanation: Total elimination debits = parent's investment carrying amount (including goodwill).

questions.questionText: The traditional definition of control for a parent company–subsidiary relationship... emphasizes:
options: Both legal form and economic substance.
Neither legal form nor economic substance.
questions.explanation: Pre-IFRS 10 definition (>50% voting) was legal/form-based.

questions.questionText: A parent need not present consolidated financial statements if it meets all the following conditions:
options: It is a wholly-owned subsidiary or is a partially-owned subsidiary of another entity and all its other owners.
Its debt or equity instruments are not traded in a public market
It did not file, nor is it in the process of filing, its financial statements with a securities commission...
An investor controls an investee when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns...
questions.explanation: Exact exemption conditions from IFRS 10.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true according to IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements issued by IASB?
options: An investor controls an investee when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns... through its power over the investee
An investor has power over an investee when the investor has existing rights...
An investor is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns... as a result of the investee’s performance.
A parent shall prepare consolidated financial statements using different accounting policies...
questions.correctAnswer: A. An investor controls an investee when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns... through its power over the investee
questions.explanation: Core definition of control (IFRS 10.6–8).

questions.questionText: In a working paper elimination... the subtotal of the debits to the subsidiary’s stockholders’ equity accounts equals the:
options: Current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
Current fair value of the subsidiary’s total net assets, including goodwill.
Balance of the parent company’s investment ledger account.
Carrying amount of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets
questions.correctAnswer: D. Carrying amount of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets
questions.explanation: Subsidiary equity is eliminated at book value.

questions.questionText: In the working paper for consolidated balance sheet... the total of the Eliminations column is equal to:
options: The current fair value of the subsidiary’s identifiable net assets.
The total stockholder’s equity of the subsidiary.
