questions.questionText: During 2012, the accounts receivable turnover rate for Upward Company increased from 10 to 15 times per year. Which one of the following statements is the most likely explanation for the change?
options: The company has decreased sales to its most credit worthy customers.
The company's credit department has followed up with customers whose account balances are past due in order to generate quicker collections.
The company has increased the amount of time customers have to pay their accounts before they are past due.
The company has extended credit to more risky customers in order to increase sales.
questions.correctAnswer: The company's credit department has followed up with customers whose account balances are past due in order to generate quicker collections.
questions.explanation: An increase in the turnover rate indicates that accounts receivable are being collected more quickly. Effective collection efforts directly cause this.

questions.questionText: The following information was presented in the balance sheet of Diablo Company as of December 31, 2012: Trade accounts receivable, net of allowance for doubtful accounts of $255,000; [$1,700,000]. Which one of the following statements is true?
options: The net realizable value Diablo's accounts receivable is $1,700,000
The balance in the Accounts Receivable account in Diablo's general ledger is $1,700,000
Diablo expects to collect only $1,445,000 from its customers
Diablo expects that $1,855,000 of accounts receivable will be collected after year end
questions.correctAnswer: The net realizable value Diablo's accounts receivable is $1,700,000
questions.explanation: The presentation 'accounts receivable, net of allowance... [$1,700,000]' means that $1,700,000 is the net realizable value (Accounts Receivable minus Allowance). So Gross AR = $1,700,000 + $255,000 = $1,955,000.

questions.questionText: Bradford Corp. reported net credit sales of $3,200,000 and cost of goods sold of $2,600,000 for 2012. On January 1, 2012, accounts receivable was $450,000. Amounts owed by customers increased by $50,000 during 2012. Rounding to two decimal places, what is Bradford's receivable turnover rate for 2012?
questions.explanation: Ending AR = Beginning AR + Increase = $450,000 + $50,000 = $500,000. Average AR = ($450,000 + $500,000) / 2 = $475,000. Receivable Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Average AR = $3,200,000 / $475,000 = 6.7368 ≈ 6.74.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an accurate description of the Allowance for Bad Debts?
questions.explanation: The Allowance for Bad Debts is a contra-asset account. It is offset against the Accounts Receivable asset account on the balance sheet.

questions.questionText: What effects on a retail store's accounting equation occur when it records merchandise on account, assuming the use of a perpetual inventory system?
questions.explanation: Recording a credit purchase of merchandise increases Inventory (an asset) and increases Accounts Payable (a liability).

questions.questionText: In order to determine inventory for its balance sheet, a company must count the inventory at the end of its accounting period according to:
options: both the periodic and perpetual inventory systems.
neither the periodic nor perpetual inventory systems.
questions.explanation: Under a periodic system, a physical count is required to determine ending inventory. Under a perpetual system, the inventory account is continuously updated, but a physical count is still performed periodically to verify accuracy and account for shrinkage.

questions.questionText: Which inventory cost flow method assigns the cost of the most recent items purchased to ending inventory?
questions.explanation: Under FIFO (First-In, First-Out), the oldest costs are assigned to Cost of Goods Sold, leaving the most recent costs in Ending Inventory.

questions.questionText: Silver mark Enterprises. The following information is from Silver mark's 2012 accounting records. Gross Purchases $182,000, Transportation - in 11,000 Inventory, January 1, 2012 26,500 Inventory, December 31, 2012 28,800 Purchase Returns and Allowances 8,400. Refer to the information provided for Silver mark Enterprises. How much will Silver mark report as net purchases for 2012?
questions.explanation: Net Purchases = Gross Purchases - Purchase Returns & Allowances + Transportation-In = $182,000 - $8,400 + $11,000 = $184,600.

questions.questionText: The cost of goods sold is equal to:
options: the amount of inventory on hand at the end of the accounting period
purchases less beginning inventory plus ending inventory.
the inventory account as reported on the balance sheet.
the cost of goods available for sale less ending inventory.
questions.correctAnswer: the cost of goods available for sale less ending inventory.
questions.explanation: Cost of Goods Available for Sale (Beginning Inventory + Net Purchases) is either sold (COGS) or remains on hand (Ending Inventory). Therefore, COGS = Cost of Goods Available for Sale - Ending Inventory.

questions.questionText: Which inventory cost flow method assigns the cost of the most recent items purchased to cost of goods sold?
questions.explanation: Under LIFO (Last-In, First-Out), the most recent costs are assigned to Cost of Goods Sold, leaving the oldest costs in Ending Inventory.

questions.questionText: Transportation-in is:
options: part of purchase returns and allowances.
added to transportation-out as part of the calculation of cost of goods sold.
part of the net cost of purchases.
questions.correctAnswer: part of the net cost of purchases.
questions.explanation: Transportation-in (or freight-in) is the cost to bring inventory to its place of sale and is added to the net cost of purchases when calculating Cost of Goods Sold.

questions.questionText: Billet Corporation. Billet Corporation is a merchandising company. Selected account balances are listed below. Sales $500,000, Purchases 225,000, Beginning Inventory 16,000, Ending Inventory 30,000, Operating Expenses 148,000, Income Tax Expense 10,000, Beginning Retained Earnings 53,000, Dividends 15,000. Calculate the Cost of Goods Sold for Billet Corporation.
questions.explanation: COGS = Beginning Inventory + Purchases - Ending Inventory = $16,000 + $225,000 - $30,000 = $211,000.

questions.questionText: The inventory turnover ratio is represented by which of the following formulas?
options: Cost of goods sold / average inventory
Average inventory / cost of goods sold
questions.correctAnswer: Cost of goods sold / average inventory
questions.explanation: Inventory turnover measures how many times a company sells and replaces its inventory. It is calculated as Cost of Goods Sold divided by Average Inventory.

questions.questionText: Inventory turned over seven times during the year at Prosser Electronics. Similar electronics retailers have an inventory turnover equal to twelve times per year. What explains Prosser's state of inventory management?
options: Prosser is performing much better than its competitors.
Prosser should increase the amount of goods on hand to accommodate the growth inventory demand.
Prosser sold too much inventory during the year.
Prosser needs to increase sales and decrease the amount of inventory on hand.
questions.correctAnswer: Prosser needs to increase sales and decrease the amount of inventory on hand.
questions.explanation: A lower turnover than competitors indicates Prosser is selling inventory less frequently. This could be due to low sales or carrying too much inventory. To improve, they need to boost sales and/or reduce inventory levels.

questions.questionText: For which type of merchandise would a company most likely use the specific identification method of inventory costing?
questions.explanation: Specific identification is used for high-value, unique, or easily distinguishable items, where each item's cost can be tracked individually, such as in a jewelry store.

questions.questionText: The income statement would be which part of David Jones' master budget?
questions.explanation: The master budget consists of operating budgets and financial budgets. The budgeted income statement is the culmination of the operating budgets (sales, production, etc.).

questions.questionText: Refer to the information below; Suppose 'Regal Marines' reports the following information (in hundreds of thousands of dollars); Beginning materials inventory $6 Ending materials inventory $5 Beginning work in process inventory $2 Ending work in process inventory $1 Beginning Finished goods Inventory $3 Ending finished goods inventory $5 Direct labour $30 Purchases
options: This question is incomplete in the provided text.

questions.questionText: In calculating cost of goods sold, which of the following is the manufacturer's counterpart of the retailer's purchases?
options: Total manufacturing costs incurred during the period
Total manufacturing costs to account for
questions.explanation: For a retailer, 'Purchases' is the cost of goods acquired for resale. For a manufacturer, the equivalent is 'Cost of Goods Manufactured,' which is the cost of goods completed during the period and transferred to finished goods inventory.

questions.questionText: Which is not a characteristic of management accounting information?
options: Provides detailed information about parts of the company, not just the company as a whole
questions.explanation: Management accounting emphasizes relevance and timeliness for internal decision-making, often using estimates and future projections. Financial accounting places a higher emphasis on reliability and verifiability for external users.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the cornerstone (or most critical element) of the master budget?
options: The purchases and cost of goods sold budget
questions.explanation: The sales budget is the foundation of the master budget because almost all other budgets (production, purchases, operating expenses, cash) depend on the forecasted sales level.

questions.questionText: The journal entry for recording accounts receivable is:
questions.explanation: When a credit sale is made, the company debits Accounts Receivable (an asset increasing) and credits Sales Revenue.

questions.questionText: The payment terms 2/10, n/30 tell us that
options: a 10% discount will be awarded if the payment is made within 2 days of invoice date; otherwise, the full amount is payable within 30 days of invoice date.
a 2% discount will be awarded if the payment is made within 10 months of invoice date; otherwise, the full amount is payable within 30 months of invoice date.
a 0.5% discount will be awarded if the payment is made within 10 days of invoice date; otherwise, the full amount is payable within 30 days of invoice date.
a 2% discount will be awarded if the payment is made within 10 days of invoice date; otherwise, the full amount is payable within 30 days of invoice date.
questions.correctAnswer: a 2% discount will be awarded if the payment is made within 10 days of invoice date; otherwise, the full amount is payable within 30 days of invoice date.
questions.explanation: Credit terms 2/10, n/30 mean a 2% discount is available if the invoice is paid within 10 days. If not, the full (net) amount is due within 30 days.

questions.questionText: The cash discount (also known as purchase discount or sale discount) is given to customers for:
questions.explanation: A cash discount is offered to encourage customers to pay their invoices promptly, improving the seller's cash flow.

questions.questionText: The accounts receivable that cannot be collected because of their bankruptcy or another reason are termed as:
questions.explanation: Accounts that are determined to be uncollectible are often referred to as bad debts or uncollectible accounts.

questions.questionText: Under allowance method, the journal entry to record uncollectible accounts expense is:
options: Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Dr. & Uncollectible Accounts Expense Cr.
Uncollectible Accounts Expense Dr. & Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Cr.
Uncollectible Accounts Expense Dr. & Accounts Receivable Cr.
Accounts Receivable Dr. & Uncollectible Accounts Expense Cr.
questions.correctAnswer: Uncollectible Accounts Expense Dr. & Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Cr.
questions.explanation: Under the allowance method, the adjusting entry to estimate bad debts debits Bad Debt Expense and credits the contra-asset account, Allowance for Doubtful Accounts.

questions.questionText: The Fortune Company uses allowance method to recognize uncollectible accounts expense. It provides you the following selected information: i. Accounts receivable on December 31, 2017: $380,000 ii. Required balance in Allowance for Doubtful Accounts account on December 31, 2017: $3,000 iii. Existing balance in Allowance for Doubtful Accounts account on December 31, 2017: $2,500. The journal entry required to recognize uncollectible accounts expense on December 31, 2017 is:
options: Dr. Bad Debt Expense $500; Cr. Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $500
Dr. Bad Debt Expense $3,000; Cr. Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $3,000
Dr. Bad Debt Expense $500; Cr. Accounts Receivable $500
Dr. Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $500; Cr. Bad Debt Expense $500
questions.correctAnswer: Dr. Bad Debt Expense $500; Cr. Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $500
questions.explanation: The required balance is $3,000, and the existing credit balance is $2,500. The adjustment needed is $500 ($3,000 - $2,500) to bring the allowance to the correct balance.

questions.questionText: Allowance for doubtful accounts is an example of:
questions.explanation: The Allowance for Doubtful Accounts is a contra-asset account because it has a credit balance and is subtracted from the Accounts Receivable asset account on the balance sheet.

questions.questionText: Under allowance method, the journal entry to write off an uncollectible account is:
options: Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Dr. & Accounts receivable Cr.
Accounts receivable Dr. & Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Cr.
Uncollectible Accounts Expense Dr. & Accounts Receivable Cr.
Accounts Receivable Dr. & Uncollectible Accounts Expense Cr.
questions.correctAnswer: Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Dr. & Accounts receivable Cr.
questions.explanation: Writing off a specific account under the allowance method removes the receivable and reduces the allowance. It does not affect expense or total assets/net income at the time of write-off.

questions.questionText: Under direct write off method, the journal entry to recognize uncollectible accounts expense is:
options: Uncollectible Accounts Expense Dr.; Sales Cr.
Uncollectible Accounts Expense Dr.; Accounts Receivable Cr.
Accounts Receivable Dr.; Uncollectible Accounts Expense Cr.
questions.correctAnswer: Uncollectible Accounts Expense Dr.; Accounts Receivable Cr.
questions.explanation: Under the direct write-off method, when an account is deemed uncollectible, Bad Debt Expense is debited and Accounts Receivable is credited.

questions.questionText: Under allowance method, the correct journal entry to reinstate a previously written off account is:
options: Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Dr.; Uncollectible accounts expense Cr.
Accounts Receivable Dr.; Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Cr.
Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Dr.; Accounts Receivable Cr.
questions.correctAnswer: Accounts Receivable Dr.; Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Cr.
questions.explanation: To reverse a previous write-off, the company debits Accounts Receivable to restore the asset and credits Allowance for Doubtful Accounts to restore the contra-asset. A separate entry records the cash collection.

questions.questionText: The correct journal entry for collection of accounts receivable is:
questions.explanation: Collecting cash from a credit customer increases cash (debit) and decreases the amount owed by the customer, Accounts Receivable (credit).

questions.questionText: A promissory note is written by:
options: a creditor in favor of a debtor
a customer in favor of another customer
a seller in favor of another seller
a debtor in favor of a creditor
questions.correctAnswer: a debtor in favor of a creditor
questions.explanation: A promissory note is a written promise made by a debtor (the maker) to pay a creditor (the payee) a specific sum of money, usually with interest, on a specified future date.

questions.questionText: In a promissory note, the debtor makes:
options: a conditional promise to pay a certain sum of money
an unconditional promise to pay a certain sum of money
a promise to pay only if able
a promise to pay in goods or services
questions.correctAnswer: an unconditional promise to pay a certain sum of money
questions.explanation: A promissory note contains an unconditional promise by the maker (debtor) to pay a definite sum of money to the payee (creditor) on demand or at a specified future date.

questions.questionText: Which of the following journal entries converts an account receivable into a note receivable?
options: Accounts Receivable Dr.; Note Receivable Cr.
Notes Receivable Dr.; Accounts Receivable Cr.
questions.correctAnswer: Notes Receivable Dr.; Accounts Receivable Cr.
questions.explanation: When a customer signs a promissory note to replace an existing accounts receivable balance, the company debits Notes Receivable (to recognize the new formal instrument) and credits Accounts Receivable (to remove the open account balance).

questions.questionText: Accounts receivable are reported in the balance sheet:
questions.explanation: Accounts receivable are reported at their net realizable value, which is the gross amount less the estimated allowance for doubtful accounts. This represents the amount expected to be collected.

questions.questionText: The John & Stewart Company provides you the following selected information: i. Balance in accounts receivable account on December 31, 2017: $70,000 ii. Balance in allowance for doubtful accounts account on December 31, 2017 after making adjusting entry for uncollectible accounts expense: $2,000 iii. Uncollectible accounts expense for the year 2017: $500. On the basis of above information, the net realizable value of accounts receivable to be shown in the balance sheet as at December 31, 2017 would be:
questions.explanation: Net Realizable Value = Accounts Receivable - Allowance for Doubtful Accounts = $70,000 - $2,000 = $68,000. The uncollectible accounts expense amount is not directly used in this calculation as the allowance balance is already given.

questions.questionText: The US Company uses sales method to estimate its credit losses. It provides you the following selected information: Total credit sales for the year 2017: $800,000; Estimated uncollectible credit sales for the year 2017: 1%; Balance in allowance for doubtful accounts account on December 31, 2017 before making adjusting entry for uncollectible accounts expense: $5,000. The uncollectible accounts expense to be reported in the income statement for the year 2017 is:
questions.explanation: Under the sales method (income statement approach), bad debt expense is calculated as a percentage of credit sales, regardless of the existing balance in the allowance account. Expense = $800,000 * 1% = $8,000.

questions.questionText: The main purpose of factoring accounts receivable is:
options: to create an additional guarantee of collection
to establish a legal proof for future use
to invest accounts receivable in another business
questions.explanation: Factoring involves selling accounts receivable to a third party (factor) at a discount to obtain cash quickly, rather than waiting for customers to pay.

questions.questionText: In a factoring with recourse, the loss resulting from bad debts is born by:
options: the organization buying the accounts receivable
the organization selling the accounts receivable
questions.correctAnswer: the organization selling the accounts receivable
questions.explanation: Factoring 'with recourse' means the seller (the organization selling the receivables) guarantees payment to the factor if the customer fails to pay. Therefore, the seller bears the loss from bad debts.

questions.questionText: In a factoring without recourse transaction, the loss resulting from bad debts is born by:
options: the organization selling the accounts receivable
the organization buying the accounts receivable
questions.correctAnswer: the organization buying the accounts receivable
questions.explanation: Factoring 'without recourse' means the factor (buyer) assumes the risk of bad debts. If the customer doesn't pay, the factor cannot demand payment from the seller.

questions.questionText: Double column cash book has two money column as follows:
options: One for discount and the other for bank.
One for discount and the other for cash.
One for cash and other for bank.
One for cash receipt and the other for cash payment.
questions.correctAnswer: One for cash and other for bank.
questions.explanation: A double column cash book typically has one column for recording cash transactions and another column for recording bank transactions.

questions.questionText: Contra entries are recorded in:
options: Cash book with discount and bank column.
questions.correctAnswer: Cash book with discount and bank column.
questions.explanation: Contra entries are transactions that affect both cash and bank accounts (e.g., cash deposited into bank, cash withdrawn from bank). They are recorded on both sides of a cash book with bank and cash columns.

questions.questionText: Office cash deposited into bank is recorded in cash book on:
options: Debit side and on the credit side
questions.correctAnswer: Debit side and on the credit side
questions.explanation: Depositing cash into the bank is a contra entry. In a cash book with bank and cash columns, it is recorded on the credit side (cash column decreases) and the debit side (bank column increases).

questions.questionText: Cash discount allowed is:
options: Recorded on the debit side of cash book
Recorded on the credit side of cash book
questions.correctAnswer: Recorded on the debit side of cash book
questions.explanation: Cash discount allowed is a loss or expense for the business. In a triple column cash book (with discount, cash, and bank columns), it is recorded on the debit side as a separate discount column.

questions.questionText: Cash withdrawn from bank for office use is recorded in cash book on:
questions.explanation: Withdrawing cash from the bank is a contra entry. In a cash book with bank and cash columns, it is recorded on the credit side (bank column decreases) and the debit side (cash column increases).

questions.questionText: Cash withdrawn from bank for personal use of the owner is recorded in cash book on:
questions.explanation: If the owner withdraws cash for personal use (drawings), it is not a contra entry because it doesn't increase office cash. It decreases the bank balance and increases drawings. It would be recorded on the credit side (bank column) and the corresponding debit is to the Drawings account, not in the cash book.

questions.questionText: Cash book is meant for recording:
questions.explanation: The cash book is a journal as well as a ledger for the cash account. It records all cash receipts and cash payments.

questions.questionText: Cash sales are recorded in:
questions.explanation: Cash sales involve receiving cash. All cash receipts, including cash sales, are recorded in the cash book.

questions.questionText: Petty cash book is used for recording:
questions.explanation: A petty cash book is used to record small, routine cash payments (like postage, office supplies) made from a petty cash fund.

questions.questionText: In case of cash book if nature of balance is not mentioned then it will be:
questions.explanation: A cash book normally has a debit balance because cash is an asset. An overdraft (credit balance) is an exception and must be specifically mentioned.

questions.questionText: Budget sales, plus target ending finished goods inventory, minus beginning finished goods inventory is equal to:
questions.explanation: The production budget formula is: Budgeted Production = Budgeted Sales + Desired Ending Finished Goods Inventory - Beginning Finished Goods Inventory.

questions.questionText: An inventory, which consists of partially worked goods or work in progress is called
questions.explanation: Work in process (WIP) inventory consists of goods that are in the production process but are not yet complete.

questions.questionText: Inventory of final goods that are not yet sold is called:
questions.explanation: Finished goods inventory consists of completed products that are ready for sale to customers.

questions.questionText: An inventory which consists of stock waiting to be used In process of manufacturing is known as
questions.explanation: Direct materials inventory refers to raw materials that are on hand and will be used in the production process.

questions.questionText: In cost accounting, types of inventory do not include
questions.explanation: Indirect materials are part of manufacturing overhead and are not typically tracked as a separate type of inventory in the three main inventory categories (Raw Materials, WIP, Finished Goods). They are often included in a 'supplies' inventory or expensed directly.

questions.explanation: Purchasing costs include all costs associated with acquiring the goods and getting them ready for sale, such as the purchase price, import duties, and freight-in (incoming freight).

questions.questionText: Cost of product failure, error prevention and appraisals can be classified under
questions.explanation: These are categories of quality costs: prevention costs (error prevention), appraisal costs (error detection), and failure costs (product failure).

questions.questionText: Activities related to coordinating, controlling and planning flow of inventory are classified as:
questions.explanation: Inventory management specifically deals with overseeing and controlling the ordering, storage, and use of inventory to ensure the right amount is available.

questions.questionText: The inventory costing method that charges the most recent costs incurred against revenue
questions.explanation: LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) assigns the most recent inventory purchase costs to Cost of Goods Sold, thus charging the most recent costs against revenue.

questions.questionText: If the merchandise inventory is being valued at cost and the price level is steadily rising, the method of costing that will yield the highest net income is:
questions.explanation: In a period of rising prices, FIFO assigns the oldest (lowest) costs to Cost of Goods Sold, resulting in lower COGS, higher gross profit, and higher net income compared to LIFO or Average Cost.

questions.questionText: One advantage of operating as a partnership would include:
options: Access to a larger amount of initial capital
Being able to raise capital through share issues
Greater power than a sole trader for decision making
questions.correctAnswer: Access to a larger amount of initial capital
questions.explanation: Unlike a sole proprietorship, a partnership combines the resources and capital of multiple owners, allowing for access to more initial capital.

questions.questionText: In normal trading circumstances, which of the following would not be found in a partner's current account?
questions.explanation: Goodwill is typically recorded in partners' capital accounts, not their current accounts. Current accounts usually track items like salaries, interest on capital, drawings, and share of residual profits/losses.

questions.questionText: Haslem and Stringer are in partnership sharing profits in a 3:2 ratio. Net profit for the year ended 31.12.20X5 was £12,000. Interest on capital was allocated as £400 to Haslem and £250 to Stringer. Stringer received a partnership salary of £5,000. How much was Haslem's share of profit?
questions.explanation: Profit after interest and salary = £12,000 - £400 - £250 - £5,000 = £6,350. This is shared 3:2. Haslem's share = (3/5) * £6,350 = £3,810.

questions.questionText: A financial statement that shows the inflows and outflows of cash during a particular period of time is known as:
questions.explanation: The statement of cash flows reports the cash generated and used during a specific period, categorized into operating, investing, and financing activities.

questions.questionText: A statement of cash flows has:
questions.explanation: The statement of cash flows is divided into three main sections: Operating Activities, Investing Activities, and Financing Activities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an operating cash flow?
options: payment of cash for operating expenses
questions.explanation: Purchasing equipment is an investing activity, as it involves the acquisition of long-term assets.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an investing cash flow?
options: purchase of marketable securities for $25,000 cash
sale of 2,500 shares of common stock for $15 each
questions.correctAnswer: sale of 2,500 shares of common stock for $15 each
questions.explanation: The sale of common stock is a financing activity, as it involves transactions with the company's owners.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a financing activity:
questions.explanation: Sale of an investment (like stocks or bonds of another company) is an investing activity, not a financing activity.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a non-cash investing and financing activity?
options: Conversion of bonds into common stock
Purchase of land by issuing common stock
Conversion of preferred stock into common stock
questions.explanation: Repayment of a loan involves cash and is a financing activity. The other options are significant transactions that do not involve cash and are disclosed separately.

questions.questionText: Significant non-cash investing and financing activities are reported in the:
options: operating activities section of statement of cash flows
investing activities section of statement of cash flows
foot notes or separate notes to the financial statements
financing activities section of statement of cash flows
questions.correctAnswer: foot notes or separate notes to the financial statements
questions.explanation: Non-cash investing and financing activities are excluded from the body of the statement of cash flows. They are disclosed in a separate schedule or in the notes to the financial statements.

questions.questionText: The following data belongs to Care Company: Accounts receivable on December 31, 2016: $60,000 Accounts receivable on December 31, 2017: $40,000 Net credit sales during the year 2017: $200,000. Based on the above information, the net cash collected from customers by Care Company during the year 2017 is:
questions.explanation: Cash collected from customers = Credit Sales + Decrease in Accounts Receivable = $200,000 + ($60,000 - $40,000) = $200,000 + $20,000 = $220,000.

questions.questionText: The following data belongs to Soft Company: Accounts receivable on December 31, 2016: $20,000 Accounts receivable on December 31, 2017: $25,000 Net credit sales during the year 2017: $100,000. Based on the above information, the total cash collected from customers by Soft Company during the year 2017 is:
questions.explanation: Cash collected from customers = Credit Sales - Increase in Accounts Receivable = $100,000 - ($25,000 - $20,000) = $100,000 - $5,000 = $95,000.

questions.questionText: Inventory on December 31, 2016: $5,000 Inventory on December 31, 2017: $3,000 Accounts payable on December 31, 2016: $12,000 Accounts payable on December 31, 2017: $15,000 Cost of goods sold for the year 2017: $50,000. Based on the above information, the net cash paid to suppliers of inventory during the year 2017 is:
questions.explanation: First, calculate Purchases = COGS + Ending Inventory - Beginning Inventory = $50,000 + $3,000 - $5,000 = $48,000. Cash paid to suppliers = Purchases + Decrease in AP? Wait, AP increased from 12k to 15k (increase of 3k), meaning they purchased more than they paid. Cash paid = Purchases - Increase in AP = $48,000 - ($15,000 - $12,000) = $48,000 - $3,000 = $45,000.

questions.questionText: Under indirect method of preparing statement of cash flows, depreciation expense affects:
questions.explanation: Under the indirect method, net income is adjusted for non-cash items. Depreciation expense is added back to net income in the operating activities section.

questions.questionText: A company sells an old piece of equipment for $5,000 cash. The book value of the equipment sold is $4,500. Under indirect method, the gain of $500 ($5,000 - $4,500) would affect:
questions.explanation: Under the indirect method, gains on the sale of assets are subtracted from net income in the operating activities section to avoid double-counting, as the entire proceeds from the sale are reported in investing activities.

questions.questionText: A company sells old plant for $12,000 cash. The book value of the plant is $7,000. This transaction would affect:
questions.explanation: The cash received ($12,000) is reported in the investing activities section. The gain ($5,000) is deducted from net income in the operating activities section under the indirect method.

questions.questionText: The John Company sells its delivery truck in current year. The relevant information is given below: Cost of delivery truck (purchased several years ago): $25,000 Book value of delivery truck: $5,000 Proceeds from sale of delivery truck: $4,000. Based on the above information, the operating activities section of the statement of cash flows of current year would be affected by:
questions.explanation: There is a loss on the sale of $1,000 ($5,000 book value - $4,000 proceeds). Under the indirect method, this loss is added back to net income in the operating activities section.

questions.questionText: Which of the following items affects net income but does not affect cash?
options: Amortization of intangible assets & bond discounts
questions.explanation: Depreciation, amortization, and depletion are all non-cash expenses. They reduce net income but do not involve an outflow of cash in the current period.

questions.questionText: The indirect method of preparing a statement of cash flows is also known as:
questions.explanation: The indirect method is sometimes called the reconciliation method because it starts with net income and reconciles it to net cash provided by operating activities.

questions.questionText: The following information belongs to Noor Merchandising Company: Net income: $25,000 Depreciation expenses: $2,000 Loss on sale of equipment: $100 Proceeds from sale of equipment: $500 Increase in accounts receivable: $1,000 Increase in accounts payable: $2,000 Decrease in inventory: $400. Based on the above information, the net cash provided by operating activities is:
questions.explanation: Start with Net Income: $25,000. Add back depreciation: +$2,000. Add back loss on sale: +$100. Adjust for changes in WC: Increase in AR (use cash) -$1,000; Decrease in Inventory (generates cash) +$400; Increase in AP (generates cash) +$2,000. Total = $25,000 + $2,000 + $100 - $1,000 + $400 + $2,000 = $28,500.

questions.questionText: The statement of cash flows is designed with the purpose of helping users to assess each of the following, except:
options: the major sources of cash receipts during the period
the reasons why net cash flows from operating activities differ from net income
the ability of a entity to remain liquid
questions.explanation: The statement of cash flows helps assess liquidity, solvency, and financial flexibility. Profitability is primarily assessed using the income statement.

questions.questionText: The Northern Company reported income tax expense of $30,500 on its income statement for the year December 31, 2017. The comparative balance sheet of the company showed that income tax payable on December 31, 2016 and December 31, 2017 was $4,000 and $6,500 respectively. Based on the above information, cash payment for the income tax during the year 2017 was:
questions.explanation: Cash paid for taxes = Income Tax Expense + Decrease in Tax Payable - Increase in Tax Payable. Here, payable increased from $4,000 to $6,500 (increase of $2,500). So cash paid = Expense - Increase in liability = $30,500 - $2,500 = $28,000.

questions.questionText: The land account was debited by $60,000 and credited by $25000 during the current year. The income statement reported a loss on sale of land in the amount of $2,000. All transactions related to land account was cash transactions. These transactions would be shown in the statement of cash flows as:
options: $60,000 cash provided by investing activities, and $25,000 cash disbursed for investing activities
$23,000 cash provided by investing activities, and $60,000 cash disbursed for investing activities
$25,000 cash provided by investing activities, and $60,000 cash disburser for investing activities
$27,000 cash provided by investing activities, and $60,000 cash disbursed for investing activities
questions.correctAnswer: $23,000 cash provided by investing activities, and $60,000 cash disbursed for investing activities
questions.explanation: The debit of $60,000 represents a purchase of land, a cash outflow for investing. The credit of $25,000 represents a sale of land. The cash inflow from the sale is calculated using the book value and loss. If the credit was $25,000 and loss was $2,000, the book value was $27,000. The cash received was $25,000. So investing inflow is $25,000, outflow is $60,000. But the option says $23,000 inflow, which is incorrect. Let's recalc: Credit to Land account is $25,000. This represents the cost of the land sold. If the loss on sale is $2,000, then the cash received = Book Value - Loss = $25,000 - $2,000 = $23,000. So, cash inflow from sale = $23,000. Cash outflow for purchase = $60,000. So statement shows $23,000 inflow and $60,000 outflow.

questions.questionText: A person who purchases common stock of a corporation is known as:
questions.explanation: An individual who owns common stock in a corporation is called a common stockholder or common shareholder.

questions.questionText: A person who purchases preferred stock of a corporation is known as:
questions.explanation: An individual who owns preferred stock is called a preferred stockholder.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is not true about preferred stock?
options: The rate of dividend is usually fixed
Stockholders always have a voting right
Stockholders' usually have a preference as to assets upon liquidation of the corporation
Stockholders' usually have a preference as to dividends
questions.correctAnswer: Stockholders always have a voting right
questions.explanation: Preferred stockholders generally do not have voting rights. Common stockholders typically have voting rights.

questions.questionText: Who is known as the real owner of the corporation?
questions.explanation: Common stockholders are the residual owners of the corporation. They bear the ultimate risk and have a claim on assets after all debts and preferred claims are satisfied.

questions.questionText: According to current standards, mandatorily redeemable preferred stock is required to be reported as:
questions.explanation: Mandatorily redeemable preferred stock, where the issuer is required to redeem the shares at a fixed date, has characteristics of debt and is reported as a liability, not equity.

questions.questionText: The shares of common and preferred stock that have been issued and outstanding are reported in which section of balance sheet?
questions.explanation: All issued and outstanding shares, whether common or preferred, are reported in the stockholders' equity section of the balance sheet.

questions.questionText: Any unpaid dividend is carried forward to the future periods for which type of stock?
questions.explanation: For cumulative preferred stock, any dividends that are not declared in a given year accumulate (dividends in arrears) and must be paid before any dividends can be paid to common stockholders.

questions.questionText: The Southern company issued 5,000 shares of its $10 par value common stock. These shares were issued at a price of $25 per share. The correct journal entry to record this transaction is:
options: Common stock $50,000 Dr; Additional paid - in capital - common stock $75,000 Dr; Cash $125,000 Cr.
Cash $125,000 Dr; Common stock $50,000 Cr; Additional paid - in capital - common stock $75,000 Cr.
questions.correctAnswer: Cash $125,000 Dr; Common stock $50,000 Cr; Additional paid - in capital - common stock $75,000 Cr.
questions.explanation: Cash received is 5,000 * $25 = $125,000. Common stock is credited at par value: 5,000 * $10 = $50,000. The excess over par ($15 per share, total $75,000) is credited to Additional Paid-in Capital.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not affected as a result of stock split?
options: Par value of total shares outstanding
questions.correctAnswer: Par value of total shares outstanding
questions.explanation: In a stock split, the number of shares increases, and the par value per share decreases proportionally. The total par value of outstanding shares remains the same.

questions.questionText: The following information has been extracted from the balance sheet of Washington Corporation as on December 31, 2017: Number of shares of common stock authorized: 200,000 shares; Number of shares of common stock issued and outstanding: 80,000 shares; Par value per share: $10. On January 1, 2018, the board of directors proposed a 7- for- 5 stock split which was approved. 7- for- 5 stock split would increase the number of shares issued and outstanding by:
questions.explanation: In a 7-for-5 split, you get 7 shares for every 5 held. New shares = (7/5) * 80,000 = 112,000 shares. The increase is 112,000 - 80,000 = 32,000 shares.

questions.questionText: Which of the following cannot be a component of stockholders' equity section of the balance sheet?
questions.explanation: A long-term loan is a liability, not a component of stockholders' equity.

questions.questionText: Sometime companies buyback their own shares which are known as:
questions.explanation: When a corporation buys back its own previously issued shares, those shares are called treasury stock.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about treasury stock?
options: Shares held as treasury stock are not entitled to dividends
Shares held as treasury stock are not entitled to assets upon liquidation
Shares held as treasury stock include shares that has been retired or cancelled
Shares held as treasury stock has no voting right
questions.correctAnswer: Shares held as treasury stock include shares that has been retired or cancelled
questions.explanation: Treasury stock refers to shares that were issued and subsequently reacquired but not retired. Retired or cancelled shares no longer exist and are not classified as treasury stock.

questions.questionText: The US Company repurchased its own shares of common stock. The relevant information is given below: Number of shares repurchased: 5,000 shares Par value per share of US Company: $10 The price at which shares were repurchased: $20 per share. Based on the above information, the journal entry to record the repurchase of 5,000 shares under cost method would be:
options: Treasury stock 100,000 Dr; Common stock 50,000 Cr; Additional paid-in capital 50,000 Cr.
questions.explanation: Under the cost method, treasury stock is recorded at the cost of reacquisition. Cost = 5,000 shares * $20 = $100,000. The entry is a debit to Treasury Stock and a credit to Cash for $100,000.

questions.questionText: Book value per share of common stock = ?
options: Total assets/No. of shares of common stock outstanding
Net income/No. of shares of common stock outstanding
(Stockholders' equity - Preferred stock)/No. of shares of common stock outstanding
Stockholders' equity/No. of shares of preferred stock outstanding
questions.correctAnswer: (Stockholders' equity - Preferred stock)/No. of shares of common stock outstanding
questions.explanation: Book value per common share represents the amount of equity available to common shareholders, calculated as total stockholders' equity less any preferred claims, divided by the number of common shares outstanding.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors may affect the market price of preferred stock?
options: Rate of interest on debt securities
questions.explanation: The market price of preferred stock is influenced by its dividend rate, prevailing interest rates (which affect yield comparisons), and any special features like convertibility or callability.

questions.questionText: Treasury stock is a(n)
questions.explanation: Treasury stock is a contra-equity account because it has a debit balance and is subtracted from total stockholders' equity.

questions.questionText: The following information has been extracted from the balance sheet of London Corporation as on December 31, 2017: Total stockholders' equity: $25,000,000; Preferred stock (issued and outstanding): $5,000,000; Average No. of shares of common stock outstanding: 2,000,000 shares. On the basis of above information, the book value per share of common stock is:
questions.explanation: Equity available to common shareholders = Total Equity - Preferred Stock = $25,000,000 - $5,000,000 = $20,000,000. Book value per share = $20,000,000 / 2,000,000 shares = $10.00.

questions.questionText: Dividends in arrears on cumulative preferred stock are disclosed as:
questions.explanation: Dividends in arrears are not a legal liability until declared by the board. They are disclosed in the notes to the financial statements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is not true about common stock of a large, publicly owned corporation?
options: The shares may be transferred from one stockholder to another
Stockholders have voting rights in the election of the board of directors
Stock holders have cumulative right to receive dividends
After issuance, the market value of the stock is unrelated to its par value
questions.correctAnswer: Stock holders have cumulative right to receive dividends
questions.explanation: Common stockholders do not have a cumulative right to dividends. They receive dividends only if declared by the board, and any missed dividends do not accumulate.

questions.questionText: If a partner cannot clear his debts on dissolution, the other partners must clear these debts in the following manner:
options: In the ratio of their last agreed capital balance
Debts should not be cleared by other partners
questions.correctAnswer: In the ratio of their last agreed capital balance
questions.explanation: Under the principle of 'partners share losses in the profit-sharing ratio,' but if a partner is insolvent, the loss from his capital deficiency is borne by the solvent partners in the ratio of their last agreed capitals.

questions.questionText: The main account for dealing with partnership dissolution would be:
questions.explanation: A realization account is opened to record the sale of non-cash assets, payment of liabilities, and the resulting profit or loss on dissolution of a partnership.

questions.questionText: Yates & Wells were in partnership sharing profit and losses equally. They admit Sparks as a partner and decide to share profits equally between the three partners. Goodwill is valued at £60,000 but is to be immediately written off. The effect of this on Yates' capital would be to:
questions.explanation: Goodwill is valued at £60,000. Old partners (Yates & Wells) share this in old ratio (1:1) when brought in. Yates gets £30,000 credit. Then it is written off in new ratio (1:1:1). Yates' share of write-off = £20,000. Net effect on Yates = +£30,000 - £20,000 = +£10,000 increase? That yields an increase. But the answer key says A, decrease. Let's think: If goodwill is written off immediately, the net effect on capital is zero. But the process: Credit old partners for goodwill, then debit all partners (including new) for write-off. Yates: +30,000 (credit) - 20,000 (debit) = +10,000. So his capital increases by 10,000. Option C says increase by £10,000. The answer key for 193 is A. There might be confusion. In some methods, if goodwill is not brought in cash but adjusted, the net effect might be a decrease if the new partner's share of goodwill is borne by the old partners. I'll stick with the net effect calculation based on standard practice: Net increase for Yates is £10,000.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would not be found in a partnership appropriation account?
options: Interest on loan by partner to partnership
questions.correctAnswer: Interest on loan by partner to partnership
questions.explanation: Interest on a partner's loan to the partnership is a charge against profit (expense) and is recorded in the Profit and Loss account, not the Appropriation account. Appropriation deals with the distribution of profit after this charge.

questions.questionText: If partners maintain both fixed capital and current accounts, which of the following would normally be credited to a partner's capital account?
questions.explanation: With fixed capitals, permanent changes like revaluation profits/losses and goodwill adjustments are typically made to the partners' capital accounts, not current accounts. Interest on capital and salaries go to current accounts.

questions.questionText: A debit balance on a partner's current account must indicate that:
options: Drawings are higher than the profit share for that year
They have withdrawn more than they have earned in the partnership
They have a credit balance on their capital account
questions.correctAnswer: They have withdrawn more than they have earned in the partnership
questions.explanation: A debit balance in a partner's current account means that the partner's drawings exceed their share of profits and other credits (like salaries, interest on capital) for the period.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would not appear in a limited company's appropriation account?
questions.explanation: The appropriation account for a limited company shows how the profit for the year is distributed (dividends, transfers to reserves). A transfer to a revaluation reserve arises from revaluing assets, not from profit appropriation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is not true?
options: Capital contributions do not have to be equal from each partner
Interest on capital is a reward for the different amounts of work partners may perform
Not all partners can have limited liability in a limited partnership
The partnership agreement will override the 1890 Partnership Act
questions.correctAnswer: Interest on capital is a reward for the different amounts of work partners may perform
questions.explanation: Interest on capital is a return on the capital invested, not a reward for work performed. Salaries or profit shares typically compensate for work.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a requirement made on a firm becoming a public limited company?
options: It must have the words 'public limited company' or the abbreviation 'plc' after its name
Shares must be offered for sale on the Stock exchange
An authorized capital of at least £50,000
questions.correctAnswer: Shares must be offered for sale on the Stock exchange
questions.explanation: A public limited company (plc) can offer its shares to the public, but it is not a requirement that they be listed or traded on a stock exchange. Listing is a separate decision.

questions.questionText: A company has issued 50,000, £1 ordinary shares and 60,000 5% preference shares of £1 each. If profits available for dividends are £5,000 and the firm wishes to give out all available profits as dividends then the amount given out per ordinary share would be:
questions.explanation: Preference dividend = 60,000 shares * £1 * 5% = £3,000. Profit remaining for ordinary dividends = £5,000 - £3,000 = £2,000. Dividend per ordinary share = £2,000 / 50,000 shares = £0.04.

questions.questionText: The accounting cycle starts with the:
questions.explanation: The accounting cycle begins with analyzing source documents and business transactions to determine their effect before they are recorded in the journal.

questions.questionText: After proper analysis, the business transaction is recorded in journal in a:
questions.explanation: The journal, also known as the book of original entry, records transactions in the order they occur chronologically before posting to the ledger.

questions.questionText: In accounting/bookkeeping, the term posting refers to:
options: transfer of information from ledger to trial balance
transfer of entries from journal to ledger
preparation of financial statements from trial balance
questions.correctAnswer: transfer of entries from journal to ledger
questions.explanation: Posting is the process of transferring debit and credit entries from the journal to the respective accounts in the general ledger.

questions.questionText: The Fast Company purchases land for $12,000. The payment is made by issuing 1,200 shares of common stock of $10 each. The proper journal entry for this transaction would be:
questions.explanation: Since land is acquired by issuing stock, the entry is to debit Land (increase asset) and credit Common Stock (increase equity) for the par value of the shares issued.

questions.questionText: The collection or group of accounts in an organization is known as:
questions.explanation: The general ledger is the complete set of all accounts maintained by a company, serving as the primary source of data for financial statements.

questions.questionText: The right hand side of a T-account is termed as:
questions.explanation: By convention, the left side of a T-account is the debit side, and the right side is the credit side.

questions.questionText: A credit may signify:
options: an increase in a liability account
a decrease in a liability account
an increase in an asset account
an increase in an expense account
questions.correctAnswer: an increase in a liability account
questions.explanation: Credits increase liability, equity, and revenue accounts, while they decrease asset and expense accounts.

questions.questionText: A form or statement that lists the titles and balances of ledger accounts at a given date is known as:
questions.explanation: A trial balance is an internal report that lists all ledger accounts and their balances at a specific point in time to check the equality of debits and credits.

questions.questionText: The receipt of cash from customers to whom the goods have already been sold on credit would be recorded by a:
options: debit to cash account & credit to accounts payable account
debit to cash account & credit to accounts receivable account
debit to accounts payable account & credit to cash account
debit to accounts receivable account and credit to cash account
questions.correctAnswer: debit to cash account & credit to accounts receivable account
questions.explanation: Receiving cash from a credit customer increases Cash (debit) and decreases the amount owed by the customer, Accounts Receivable (credit).

questions.questionText: The trial balance in which total debits equal total credits provides a proof that:
options: the transactions have been correctly analyzed and recorded in proper accounts
the correct debit and credit balances have been computed for each account
no transaction has been completely omitted during the posting process
questions.explanation: A balanced trial balance proves that the total of all debit balances equals the total of all credit balances in the ledger, but it does not guarantee that no errors were made.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is used to compute the net income for a specific period?
questions.explanation: The income statement summarizes revenues and expenses over a period to arrive at net income or net loss.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is helpful in determining the financial position of the business at a specific date?
questions.explanation: The balance sheet, also known as the statement of financial position, reports a company's assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time.

questions.questionText: A statement that shows the changes in the amount of retained earnings during a specific period is known as:
questions.explanation: The statement of retained earnings reconciles the beginning and ending retained earnings balance by showing additions (net income) and deductions (dividends).

questions.questionText: The amount of retained earnings at the end of a period is equal to:
options: Retained earnings at the beginning of the period + Dividends declared - Net income
Net income + Dividends declared - Retained earnings at the beginning of the period
Retained earnings at the beginning of the period + Net income - Dividends declared
Retained earnings at the beginning of the period + Net income - Operating expenses
questions.correctAnswer: Retained earnings at the beginning of the period + Net income - Dividends declared
questions.explanation: Ending retained earnings is calculated by adding net income (which increases retained earnings) to the beginning balance and subtracting any dividends declared.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a fixed asset?
questions.explanation: Fixed assets (Property, Plant, and Equipment) are long-term tangible assets used in operations. Inventory is a current asset held for sale.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an intangible asset?
questions.explanation: Intangible assets lack physical substance (like patents and goodwill). Prepaid expenses are current assets representing payments made in advance for future benefits.

questions.questionText: Which of the following financial statements is generally prepared first?
questions.explanation: The income statement is prepared first to determine net income, which is then used to prepare the statement of retained earnings. The ending retained earnings is then used on the balance sheet.

questions.questionText: ABC is a profitable company. Which of the following journal entries would it make to close its income summary account?
options: Credit income summary account & debit capital stock account
Debit income summary account & credit capital stock account
Debit income summary account & credit retained earnings account
Credit income summary account & debit retained earnings account
questions.correctAnswer: Debit income summary account & credit retained earnings account
questions.explanation: For a profitable company, the Income Summary account has a credit balance. To close it, you debit Income Summary and credit Retained Earnings, transferring the net income.

questions.questionText: Which if the following accounts is not closed to income summary account at the end of the accounting period?
questions.explanation: Accumulated Depreciation is a contra-asset account (a permanent or real account) that appears on the balance sheet. Only temporary accounts (revenues, expenses, and dividends) are closed.

questions.questionText: The steps of the operating cycle for a retailer usually take place in which order?
options: Purchases of merchandise → Sale of merchandise on account → Collection of the receivables
Sale of merchandise on account → Purchases of merchandise → Collection of the receivables
Collection of the receivables → Purchases of merchandise → Sale of merchandise on Account
Purchases of merchandise → Collection of the receivables → Sale of merchandise on Account
questions.correctAnswer: Purchases of merchandise → Sale of merchandise on account → Collection of the receivables
questions.explanation: The operating cycle for a retailer typically begins with purchasing inventory, then selling it on account, and finally collecting cash from customers.

questions.questionText: The Rebecca Company purchased equipment for $60,000 cash. What is the effect on total assets?
options: Cannot be determined from this limited information.
questions.explanation: Purchasing equipment for cash increases one asset (Equipment) and decreases another asset (Cash) by the same amount, resulting in no net change in total assets.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of an accrued liability?
options: An insurance policy that expires in a future period has been acquired.
Equipment that will benefit several periods has been purchased.
Rent that has been incurred, but have not been paid at the end of the period.
Supplies are purchased and used over several months.
questions.correctAnswer: Rent that has been incurred, but have not been paid at the end of the period.
questions.explanation: An accrued liability represents an expense that has been incurred but not yet paid (or recorded). Unpaid rent incurred is a classic example.

questions.questionText: X-company issued a 4 years term bond with a par value of 400,000, which pays 8% interest payable semi-annually to yield 10% effective rate. The proceeds of this bond is
options: The same as the par value
questions.explanation: When the stated interest rate (8%) is less than the effective market rate (10%), the bond will be issued at a discount, meaning the proceeds are less than the par value.

questions.questionText: Portion of bonds, mortgage notes, and other long-term indebtedness that matures within the next fiscal year is represented as:
questions.explanation: The portion of long-term debt that is due within the next year is classified as a current liability, often called 'Current Maturity of Long-Term Debt'.

questions.questionText: Abebe Company issues Br. 2,500,000, 6%, 5- year bonds dated January 1, 2017. The bonds pay interest semiannually on July 1 and January 1. The bonds are issued to yield 6%. What is the proceed from the bond issue?
questions.explanation: Since the stated rate (6%) equals the effective yield rate (6%), the bonds are issued at par value. Therefore, the proceeds are equal to the par value of Br. 2,500,000.

questions.questionText: Assume the leasee company 'A' agreed to lease a property from a leaser company 'B'. Down payment made by company 'A' is 100,000 br. and agreed to add br. 50,000 for 4 years at the end of every year. Company 'A' paid 20,000 br. for commission the estimated cost for dismantling and restoration after 4 years is 60,000 (material). The incremental borrowing rate is 10%. Calculate the right to use an asset?
questions.explanation: The Right-of-Use asset is calculated as the present value of lease payments plus any initial direct costs and estimated restoration costs. PV of annual payments (50,000 for 4 years @10%) = 50,000 * 3.16986 = 158,493. Plus down payment (100,000) + commission (20,000) + PV of restoration cost (60,000 * 0.68301 = 40,981). Total = 158,493 + 100,000 + 20,000 + 40,981 = 319,474.

questions.questionText: How much is the initial balance of lease liability?
questions.explanation: The initial lease liability is the present value of the future lease payments, excluding the down payment. PV of 50,000 for 4 years at 10% = 50,000 * 3.169865 = 158,493.

questions.questionText: Calculate the interest expense for the end of the first year?
questions.explanation: Interest expense is calculated on the outstanding lease liability. Interest = 158,493 * 10% = 15,849.

questions.questionText: Calculate the balance of lease liability at the end of year one?
questions.explanation: Lease liability at end of year 1 = Beginning liability + Interest - Payment = 158,493 + 15,849 - 50,000 = 124,342.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a characteristic of the balance sheet?
options: It is prepared for the time period.
The balance sheet provides information useful in assessing liquidity
The balance sheet reports the change in financial position
The major classifications of the balance sheet are assets, liabilities, and owners' equity
questions.correctAnswer: It is prepared for the time period.
questions.explanation: The balance sheet reports financial position at a specific point in time (a date), not for a time period. The income statement and statement of cash flows cover a period of time.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is false regarding bank reconciliation?
options: Deduct understatement of error during cash receipt.
Deduct Overstatement of error during cash receipt.
Add Overstatement of error during cash payment.
questions.explanation: Outstanding checks are deducted from the bank balance, not the book balance. The question is ambiguous, but all options relate to book adjustments except C. Outstanding checks are a bank reconciliation item, but the statement 'Deduct outstanding cheque' is not false; it's a true step in reconciling the bank balance. The false one might be A or B depending on context. Based on the answer key (A), deducting an understatement error during cash receipt is incorrect procedure. If cash receipts were understated, you would add to the book balance, not deduct.

questions.questionText: Which of the following order is correct for Revenue recognition?
options: Identifying the contract, identifying separate performance obligation, determining the transaction price, allocate the transaction price and recognize revenue.
Identifying the contract, determining the transaction price, identifying separate performance obligation, allocate the transaction price and recognize revenue.
Identifying the contract, allocate the transaction price, identifying separate performance obligation, determining the transaction price and recognize revenue.
Identifying the contract, identifying separate performance obligation, allocate the transaction price, recognize revenue and determining the transaction price.
questions.correctAnswer: Identifying the contract, identifying separate performance obligation, determining the transaction price, allocate the transaction price and recognize revenue.
questions.explanation: IFRS 15 specifies the five-step model for revenue recognition: 1. Identify the contract, 2. Identify performance obligations, 3. Determine transaction price, 4. Allocate price, 5. Recognize revenue when obligations are satisfied.

questions.questionText: In the statement of cash flows, payments to acquire debt instruments of other entities should be classified as cash out flows for:
questions.explanation: Purchasing debt instruments (like bonds) of other entities is an investing activity, as it involves acquiring an asset for investment purposes.

questions.questionText: ABC Co uses the percentage of completion method of accounting for its revenues from construction activities. In 2013, the company has a project in process with an estimated remaining cost of $300,000 on Dec 31, end of the fiscal year. The contract price was $1,000,000. Cost incurred to date (as of Dec 31, 2013) total $500,000. If the project was 50% complete as of Dec 31, 2012, what is the amount of revenues from construction to be recognized in 2013?
questions.explanation: Total estimated costs = Costs incurred to date + Estimated remaining costs = $500,000 + $300,000 = $800,000. Total estimated profit = $1,000,000 - $800,000 = $200,000. In 2012, they were 50% complete, so revenue recognized in 2012 = 50% * $1,000,000 = $500,000. In 2013, % complete = Costs incurred to date / Total estimated costs = $500,000 / $800,000 = 62.5%. Revenue recognized by end of 2013 = 62.5% * $1,000,000 = $625,000. Revenue for 2013 = $625,000 - $500,000 = $125,000.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not an element of the profit or loss statement?
questions.explanation: Dividends are distributions of profit to owners and are not an expense. They are reported in the statement of changes in equity, not the profit or loss statement (income statement).

questions.questionText: Cash receipts from issuance of equity securities, bonds, and notes are referred to as:
options: Cash out flow from financing activities
questions.explanation: Issuing equity or debt securities to raise funds is a financing activity. Cash received from these transactions is a cash inflow from financing.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is ODD? The liability arises from
questions.explanation: Liabilities typically arise from legally enforceable obligations like contracts, laws, or court decisions. 'Past experience' might lead to a constructive obligation, but it is less definitive and is the odd one out compared to the others which are explicit sources.

questions.questionText: What is the accounting method that should be applied, If the business model is held to collect and sale and cash flow character is other than Solely principal and interest?
options: Fair value through OCI or PL
questions.explanation: Under IFRS 9, if the business model is to both collect and sell, and the cash flows are not solely principal and interest (SPPI), the instrument is measured at Fair Value Through Profit or Loss (FVTPL).

questions.questionText: When applying the equity method, an investor should report dividends from the investee as:
options: A reduction in the investment account
An increase in the investment account
questions.correctAnswer: A reduction in the investment account
questions.explanation: Under the equity method, dividends received from the investee are considered a return on investment and reduce the carrying amount of the investment account (debit Cash, credit Investment in Investee).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a current liability?
questions.explanation: Bonds payable are typically long-term liabilities, unless they are maturing within the next year. The other options are typical current liabilities.

questions.questionText: In a job-order costing system, the application of manufacturing overhead would be recorded as a debit to:
questions.explanation: Applied manufacturing overhead is added to Work in Process Inventory as part of the total manufacturing cost. The entry is: Debit WIP, Credit Manufacturing Overhead.

questions.questionText: Spoilage that is an inherent result of the particular production process and arises under efficient operating conditions is referred to as:
options: None of the sensors is correct
questions.explanation: Normal spoilage is the spoilage that is expected and unavoidable under efficient operating conditions. It is inherent to the production process.

questions.questionText: Classifying a cost as either direct or indirect depends upon:
options: The behavior of the cost in response to volume changes
Whether the cost is expensed the period in which its incurred
Whether the cost can be easily identified with the cost object
Whether an expenditure is avoidable or not in the future
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the cost can be easily identified with the cost object
questions.explanation: Direct costs can be easily and conveniently traced to a specific cost object, while indirect costs cannot.

questions.questionText: When bakery transfers goods from the Baking Department to the Decorating Department, the accounting entry is
options: Work in Process-BakingDepartment XXX Work in Process-DecoratingDepartment XXX
Work in Process-DecoratingDepartment XXX Accounts Payable XXX
Work in Process-DecoratingDepartment XXX Work in Process-BakingDepartment XXX
Work in Process-BakingDepartment XXX Accounts Payable XXX
questions.correctAnswer: Work in Process-DecoratingDepartment XXX Work in Process-BakingDepartment XXX
questions.explanation: When goods are transferred from one department to the next, the receiving department's WIP is debited, and the transferring department's WIP is credited.

questions.questionText: Which of the following measures the difference between what is paid for a given quantity of materials and what should have been paid according the standard that has been set is?
questions.explanation: Material price variance is the difference between the actual price paid for materials and the standard price, multiplied by the actual quantity purchased.

questions.questionText: In process costing system, the sum of beginning work in process cost and total manufacturing cost started during the current period is known as?
options: Work done in the current period
questions.explanation: Total costs to account for equals the sum of Beginning WIP inventory costs and all manufacturing costs added during the current period.

questions.questionText: A joint cost allocation technique which uses the relative weight, volume or other measure is called?
questions.explanation: The physical measure method allocates joint costs based on a physical measure such as weight, volume, or quantity of the joint products.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the main goal of financial management?
questions.explanation: The primary goal of financial management is to maximize shareholder wealth, which is reflected in the market price of the firm's shares.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is concerned with the mix or composition of the sources of raising the funds required by the firm.
questions.explanation: Financing decisions involve determining the optimal capital structure, i.e., the mix of debt and equity used to finance the firm's operations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following give an idea of the firm's ability to pay off debts that are maturing within a year.
questions.explanation: Liquidity ratios, such as the current ratio and quick ratio, measure a firm's ability to meet its short-term obligations as they come due.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true regarding the cost of capital of a firm?
options: It is the firm's required rate of return.
It is the minimum rate of return expected by its investors.
It is a maximum rate of return to cover the cost of generating funds for investments.
It is the minimum rate of return required by suppliers of the firm's capital.
questions.correctAnswer: It is the minimum rate of return required by suppliers of the firm's capital.
questions.explanation: The cost of capital represents the minimum rate of return a firm must earn on its investments to satisfy its investors (both debt and equity holders).

questions.questionText: Capital budgeting decisions require special attention because of the following reasons, except:
options: They affect the risk of the firm.
They are reversible without substantial loss.
They influence the firm's growth in the long run.
They involve commitment of large amount of funds.
questions.correctAnswer: They are reversible without substantial loss.
questions.explanation: Capital budgeting decisions typically involve large sums of money, have long-term implications, and are often irreversible or very costly to reverse. They are not easily reversible without substantial loss.

questions.questionText: A portfolio comprises two securities and the expected return on them is 12% and 16% respectively. Determine return of portfolio if first security constitutes 40% of total portfolio.
questions.explanation: Portfolio return = (Weight of security 1 * Return of security 1) + (Weight of security 2 * Return of security 2) = (0.40 * 12%) + (0.60 * 16%) = 4.8% + 9.6% = 14.4%.

questions.questionText: Your bank account pays a 6% stated annual interest rate (or APR). The interest is compounded quarterly. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: The quarterly interest rate is 1.5% and the effective annual interest rate is 3%.
The quarterly interest rate is 6% and the effective annual interest rate is greater than 6%.
The quarterly interest rate is 1.5% and the effective annual interest rate is greater than 6%.
The quarterly interest rate is 3% and the effective annual interest rate is 6%.
questions.correctAnswer: The quarterly interest rate is 1.5% and the effective annual interest rate is greater than 6%.
questions.explanation: Quarterly rate = APR / 4 = 6% / 4 = 1.5%. Effective Annual Rate (EAR) = (1 + 0.015)^4 - 1 = 6.14%, which is greater than the stated APR of 6%.

questions.questionText: Which of the following leverage is defined as the extent to which a firm's operations involve fixed operating costs.
questions.explanation: Operating leverage measures the sensitivity of operating income to changes in sales volume, arising from the presence of fixed operating costs in the firm's cost structure.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not correct about working capital and working capital management?
options: Working capital refers to the portion of firm's capital that can be immediately put to work to generate the benefits of capital investment.
It involves managing the relationship between a firm's short-term assets and liabilities.
The goal is to ensure the firm can continue operations and meet short-term debts.
Working capital is calculated as current assets minus current liabilities.
questions.correctAnswer: Working capital refers to the portion of firm's capital that can be immediately put to work to generate the benefits of capital investment.
questions.explanation: This definition is vague and more applicable to capital in general. Working capital specifically refers to the difference between current assets and current liabilities, and its management involves short-term assets and liabilities.

questions.questionText: Suppose the term of sales of ABC Company is 3/15, n/45 and annual credit sales of the company are birr 400,000, then what is the credit period and cash discount of the company respectively?
questions.explanation: Credit terms 3/15, n/45 mean the credit period (time to pay without discount) is 45 days. The cash discount is 3%. The discount amount in birr = 3% * 400,000 = 12,000 birr.

questions.questionText: The Recorded for cash dividend payment procedure is January 20, 2022, and then EX-dividend date for cash dividend payment procedure is:
questions.explanation: The ex-dividend date is typically two business days before the record date (date of record). If the record date is January 20, the ex-dividend date would be January 18 (assuming no weekends interfere).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not correct about financial forecasting of the business?
options: Financial forecasting is a force of financial managers to develop financial statements beforehand.
It is a planning process which involves forecasting of sales, assets, and financial requirements.
The first procedure of the financial forecasting is determining the assets required to meet the sales targets.
It is a pre requirement for the investment, financing, as well as dividend policy decisions of a firm.
questions.correctAnswer: The first procedure of the financial forecasting is determining the assets required to meet the sales targets.
questions.explanation: Financial forecasting typically begins with a sales forecast. The assets required are then determined based on the projected sales level.

questions.questionText: Assume asset and liability of the company is record as following at the time of preparing financial forecasting during the year. Current asset- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - birr490, 000 Long-term assets- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - bir610, 000 Current liability - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - birr510, 000 Long - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -birr290, 000. Then, what is additional funds needed (AFN) of the company to generate external source to meet its forecast?
